structure.conclusion: ENTROPY-BALANCE (owner derivation 2026-11-26, director check; CLAIMED). Setting: Y uniform on {0,1}^b, x_j = Y_{l(j)} (l surjective, Lupanov-type addressing so that CC(x) <= s for every Y, b = Theta(s log s)); M a correct MCSP[s] DTIME1 machine, accepted set of size <= 2^L, L = O(s log s); A = crossing signature (seq 17306 decomposition), R_alpha = accepted inputs with signature alpha = product of R_{alpha,j} over the block-visit parts J_{alpha,j} (cut-and-paste for a fixed blocking), disjoint over alpha. VERIFIED: (i) x|_{J} <-> Y_{l(J)} is a bijection, so log|R_{alpha,j}| >= H(Y_{I_{alpha,j}} | A = alpha); (ii) chain rule and monotonicity give >= sum_{i in I} h_i(alpha), h_i = H(Y_i | Y_{<i}, A = alpha); (iii) Z = (alpha ~ A, then uniform on R_alpha): H(Z) = H(A) + E log|R_alpha| <= L; (iv) H(Y|A) = E sum_i h_i = b - H(A). Hence L >= b + E sum_i (c_i(alpha) - 1) h_i(alpha) and, with multiplicity c_i >= r, H(A) >= (r b - L)/(r - 1). CEILING (director): since H(A) <= H(Y) = b, the balance can force at most H(A) close to b = Theta(s log s); a contradiction with a machine needs a blocking whose crossing record carries fewer than b bits (log K < b = N^{mu+o(1)}) while every information bit has multiplicity r > L/b (a constant, about 2 for Lupanov counting). Multiplicity >= 2 requires the copies of each Y_i to be read in >= 2 distinct blocks, so a machine whose work head stays in one block (block length >= its work space) has r = 1 and the balance reduces to the trivial L >= b. Generic time-t bound: log K = Theta(sqrt(t log N)) (seq 17306), so the balance reproduces exactly the CHMY regime s log s >~ sqrt t (mu > ~0.505 at t = N^{1.01}). NECESSARY USE OF q = O(1): for the folded Corollary-17 machine (seq 17279 (c); Sigma3-oracle answers folded into 2^{poly(s)} states, a correct MCSP[s] decider) every crossing entry carries poly(s) >= b bits and zero crossings give r = 1, so the balance yields no contradiction for it - any successful use must exploit that crossing entries of an O(1)-state machine carry O(log N) bits. PRECISE FORM of the owner's next step (recorded, not a new obligation): an address map l such that every O(1)-state time-N^{1.01} DTIME1 machine admits a blocking with fewer than N^{mu+o(1)} / log N crossings and multiplicity > L/b. Type: an information-complexity form of the crossing-sequence / rectangle (cut-and-paste) argument; novelty not checked. Not a gap closure.

D6 REUSE COLLAPSE UNDER RESTRICTION (repair of the D5 limit): let d_g be the number of input variables gate g depends on. Under a truly random p-restriction, a reused gate stays a non-literal, non-constant reused gate only if >= 2 of its d_g variables stay live, so Pr <= C(d_g,2) p^2 <= p^2 d_g^2/2 (union over pairs) and E[gamma(C|rho)] <= sum_{g reused} min(1, p^2 d_g^2/2). With p = N^{beta+eps/5-1}: reused gates with d_g <= N^{1-beta-eta} contribute <= N^{-2 eta}, so only WIDE reused gates (d_g > N^{1-beta-eta}) can survive. Combined with AF: if P1, P2 hold, Gap-MCSP[N^beta] has no De Morgan circuit of size N^{1+eps} with at most N^{beta-2eta} wide reused gates (Markov over rho). Sanity check (dual-rail parity): the tree has ~N/2^j reused nodes with d_g = 2^j; sum_j (N/2^j) min(1,p^2 4^j) = Theta(pN) = Theta(k) survivors, matching counterexample 1 - those survivors are exactly the wide nodes (d_g >= 1/p). REMAINING OBLIGATION (unrestricted circuits): circuits computing Gap-MCSP[N^beta] with more than N^beta wide reused gates.

statement: T56 sec.4 addendum (owner derivation, PI verified), supersedes the from-memory O(n^2) remark of 18106. (a) Original witness space over K = F_{2^r}, r = n+ceil(log2(m+1))+1: P_x(Y) = sum_z R Y^z is nonzero iff exists z; Schwartz-Zippel + union bound (2^n m/2^r < 1) give a fixed a with P_x(a) != 0 for all satisfiable x; Lambda_a(z) = prod a_i^{z_i}; unconditional, nonuniform. (b) M^{2^r-1} = [M!=0], Frobenius additive in char 2 with R in {0,1}: E(x) = sum over r copies of prod_j R(x,z_j) Lambda_a(z_j)^{2^j}; with Tr(beta) = 1, W = Tr(beta prod_j Lambda_a(z_j)^{2^j}) gives E = sum_{z-vec} W prod_j R over F2, with W poly-size; this is NP in parityP/poly (known) with O(n + log m) copies. (c) Weight size is blind on the original space over K and on the extended space over F2; only exactly normalized F2 weights on the original space remain open; the x-dependent exact weight Tr(beta P_x(a)^{-1} prod a^z) needs the exponential sum P_x(a), so the difficulty is the elimination cost. Under P=NP this parityP/poly expression collapses: no known contradiction.

statement: BLOCK NORMALIZATION OF STRUCTURE VERSUS LOCAL INFORMATION (owner question 2026-11-27; PI theorem and limits; CLAIMED, Claude family). (1) Owner observation, checked. A bag of k vertices of G becomes 2k parameters. Formal states go from 3^k to 9^k; locally admissible states stay 3^k (3 of 9 pairs (p,q) per vertex, 17922). Solution information is identical, and the coordinate change of 17923 inverts the expansion. (2) Theorem (PI). Let H be a constraint primal graph and P a partition of its variables into connected blocks of size <= t, with quotient graph H/P. Then tw(H/P) <= tw(H) <= t(tw(H/P)+1) - 1, and likewise for pathwidth. Proof: H/P is a minor of H (contract connected blocks), and treewidth is minor-monotone. For the upper bound, substitute each block into the bags of an optimal decomposition of H/P. Both bounds are attained: J of 17923 (quotient G, tw = max(tw(G),1)) and the block form G[K_2] (17922/17923, tw = 2 tw(G)+1). So the variable-level width can sit anywhere in this interval for the same quotient structure. (3) Normalized measure. Merge each block into one compound variable whose domain D_b is the set of locally admissible block states. Define the semantic width w_sem = min over decompositions of H/P of max over bags B of sum_{b in B} log_3 |D_b| (weighted treewidth with weights log|D_b|; the term is from the literature, cited from memory, unverified). w_sem depends only on H/P and the |D_b|, so it is invariant under every blockwise bijective recoding. For the prism block form, D_b has 3 elements and H/P = G, so w_sem = tw(G)+1 = the value for G itself. Structural expansion and semantic conservation are then two coordinates of one exact statement. (4) Limit. The invariance holds for block-local bijections only. A global bijection of F3^n can map a solution set of size 3^k onto F3^k x {0}, whose primal graph has no edges. So no width measure is invariant under arbitrary bijections. The only fully invariant quantity is the number of solutions (U_G(1)), which is #P-type information and says nothing about deciding (edgeless G has the most colourings). A general normalization therefore has to fix the admissible class of recodings, and block-local is the natural exact class. (5) Consequence for the universal function: U_G is invariant under blockwise recodings (monomial substitutions, 17913, Fable A2) and carries the semantics. w_sem is the matching structural invariant, and both are preserved by the whole prism pipeline. No lower bound, no running-time claim; no obligation closed.

structure.conclusion: tw(H/P) <= tw(H) <= t(tw(H/P)+1)-1 for connected blocks, both tight; semantic width invariant under blockwise bijections only

structure.conclusion: A*-REFUTER (owner construction 2026-11-26, director check; CLAIMED). u_j = 1-P_j(n,j) if P_j answers within B, else 0 (j <= K); u_{K+1}=1; other bits 0; v = 0^n if b0=0, v = e_{K+1} if b0=1. Every P_j mismatches at position j, so A* outputs b0, while DISJ(u,v)=1-b0: R refutes A* at every large n without simulating A*'s stream. L_R={<n,i>: R(1^n)_i=1} is in DTIME(m^{O(sqrt log m)}); L_R is NOT in P (unconditional): a fixed m^c-time program for L_R would be enumerated and kept active, so A* would be correct on R(1^n) - this is a time-hierarchy diagonal, nothing beyond the hierarchy theorem. CC(R(1^n)) = O(m^2) (at most 2m+2 ones: DNF of minterms), so R is non-uniformly easy; the sparse algorithm A** (store the <= K+1 one-positions of x, O(m^2) space, check them against y) solves every R-instance unconditionally. So R refutes A* only, not the class; CJSW's search-MCSP algorithm (P=NP) would also capture it.

SEED-FLOOR (proof of the D5 claim, seq 16768): if a distribution G on {0,1}^k has support size <= M (e.g. seed length l, M = 2^l), then some AND of t = floor(log2 M) + 1 <= k literals has |Pr_G - Pr_U| >= 2^{-t}: of the 2^t patterns on the first t coordinates at most M < 2^t are hit, a missed pattern has Pr_G = 0 and Pr_U = 2^{-t}. Hence fooling De Morgan formulas of size >= t with error delta forces log2 M >= log2(1/delta) - 1. In the D4/AF mechanism (error 2^{-r-2} for r surviving reused gates): seed >= r + 1, and since YES outputs G(z) o rho have circuit size <= N^beta, the support on the star coordinates is <= 2^{O(N^beta log N)}, so r <= O(N^beta log N). Consequence: every PRG instantiation of AF has polylog(1/delta)-exponent a >= 1 and covers at most N^{beta+o(1)} surviving reused gates; circuits with more surviving reuse must first be reduced by D6'/NORM.

statement: CHARACTERIZATION OF THE COMPRESSION PREMISE; ROUTE CLOSED (owner 2026-11-27; PI check; CLAIMED, Claude family). U := there is a polynomial p such that for every transition circuit f of size m with s state bits and every j = O(s), the relation b = f^{2^j}(a) has an existential EO-graph representation of size <= p(m). Claim U <-> PSPACE subset of NP/poly. (=>) The PSPACE machine's configuration b is unique, so acceptance = exists b,y: G(start(x),b,y) and acc(b); this is NP/poly (17584 encoding). (<=) Iterated circuit value with binary j (f part of the input) is in PSPACE, hence has nondeterministic poly-size circuits; hardwire f and compile them to EO-graphs (17584). Under P=NP: U <-> P=PSPACE. (=>) PSPACE subset of P/poly, then PSPACE = MA (from memory) subset of Sigma2 = P; alternatively the constructive MinGraph of 17586. (<=) trivial. Verdict: the time-hierarchy route via compact configuration spaces is closed (17586). Relativization triage, unproven: Hall/support embeddings, semiring evaluation and coefficient conservation are oracle-free finite combinatorics; the only step that touches computation structure is the compilation of a circuit into G_C (Cook-Levin locality, arithmetization type, expected to algebrize per Aaronson-Wigderson, not proved here). Semantic minimization relativizes.

structure.conclusion: U <-> PSPACE subset NP/poly; under P=NP U <-> P=PSPACE; route closed

structure.conclusion: EXCLUSION E-PLS-BLACKBOX: (a) P = NP => PLS subset FP (prefix search for x with V(F(x)) <= V(x)); so 'some PLS problem has no polynomial-time algorithm' => P != NP, the converse is not known (the target is at least as strong as P != NP). (b) Black-box query lower bounds for local search (Aldous 1983, Aaronson 2006) hold relative to every oracle, including an oracle A with P^A = NP^A, where PLS^A subset FP^A by (a) relativized; hence a black-box lower bound alone cannot imply the white-box statement or P != NP. Excluded: black-box-to-white-box transfer. Also: long improvement paths are not search hardness (binary counter: 2^m - 1 steps, end state 1...1 computable directly).

structure.conclusion: EXACT COUNTING TRANSFER to colourings and to F(G) (owner gadgets 2026-11-27; PI verification count_transfer_check.py, fg_cov_check.py; CLAIMED, Claude family). (1) Clause gadget: a or b or c -> NAE(a,b,z), NAE(not z,c,0), NAE(not z,not a,0), NAE(not z,not b,0). NAE(x,y,0) is x or y, so z = 1 forces a = b = 0 and c = 1, and z = 0 forces a or b; the extension is unique (z = not(a or b)) iff the clause holds. Table 8/8. (2) Colouring graph: reference triangle T, F, B; literal triangles (x, not x, B); one NAE triangle v1 v2 v3 with v_i adjacent to its literal (constant 0 = F). A satisfied NAE gadget has exactly 2 internal colourings, an all-equal one has none. P_{G_phi}(3) = 6 * 2^{4m} * #SAT(phi). Checked 12/12 random 3-CNF with exact colouring counts. (3) Weighted removal: Q_G(X) = sum over proper sigma of prod_v X_{v,sigma(v)}. Char != 2: weight 1/2 on one internal vertex per gadget. Char 2: over F_4 with omega^2 + omega + 1 = 0, weights v1 (1,1,1), v2 (omega,omega^2,1), v3 (omega^2,omega,1); the gadget sum is 1 on NAE inputs and 0 otherwise, verified 8/8 for all 6 choices of reference colours. (4) Projection: take the parsimonious tableau 3-CNF Psi_n of the clocked machine (branch choice recorded, idle padding, Tseitin auxiliaries determined; 17548) with free inputs x. Set G_n = colouring graph of Psi_n and let pi be: reference vertices X_{ref,c} = [c = designated colour] (removes the factor 6); positive literal vertex of x_i: X_{T} = X_{i,1}, X_{F} = X_{i,0}, X_{B} = 0; gadget weights as in (3); every other variable 1. Then pi(Q_{G_n}) = sum_x U_n(x) prod_i X_{i,x_i} = P_n over every field K with char K != 2 or omega in K. For char 2 without omega: size_K(Q) >= size_{K(omega)}(Q) >= size_{K(omega)}(P_n). Size |G_n| = O(|Psi_n|) = O(T^2), T = n^{10^9}. (5) F(G): variables x_{v,c}, y_{e,c}; EO(x_{v,1},x_{v,2},x_{v,3}) and EO(x_{u,c},x_{w,c},y_{e,c}). y_{e,c} = 1 - x_{u,c} - x_{w,c} is forced and lies in {0,1} iff not both endpoints have colour c, so the solutions are in bijection with proper colourings (checked on random graphs). Weights X_{v,c} on x_{v,c} and 1 on y give Gen_{F(G)} = Q_G, coefficient by coefficient; hence P_n = pi(Gen_{F(G_n)}). SEPARATION OF LEVELS: (i) counting transfer: established here (CLAIMED until cross-family review); (ii) arithmetic lower bound for P_n, hence for Q_{G_n} and Gen_{F(G_n)}: OpenAI's claim, unreviewed and not built; (iii) Boolean decision lower bound: none, since Q_{G_n} is a generating polynomial and the decision version is a different object (17540).

statement: EXISTENCE ELIMINATION IN CLOSED FORM (owner checkpoint 2026-11-27, active focus 'effiziente Existenzeliminierung'; PI derivation; CLAIMED, Claude family). (1) Check of the owner identity. Over F3, (w-2)^2 = 1 for w != 2 and 0 for w = 2. So Q_G(lambda) = prod_i (z0_i + (B lambda)_i - 2)^2 is the indicator of z in {0,1}^N. Reduced forms in R = F3[lambda]/(lambda_k^3 - lambda_k) are the functions on F3^r, so F_E is satisfiable iff Q_G != 0 in R. Correct. Hardness of the target: G is 3-colourable iff prod_{ab in E} (lambda_a - lambda_b)^2 != 0 in R, which is the squared graph polynomial; this is Q-form with z = lambda_a - lambda_b + 2. So deciding Q != 0 in R is NP-complete, and an efficient evaluation is exactly P = NP; there is no weaker sub-target. E_i(Q) = 1 - prod_a (1 - Q|_{lambda_i = a}) is correct for {0,1}-valued Q: it is the OR over the fibre. (2) Closure lemma (proved). Write Q = 1 - 1_U, where U is the union of the affine hyperplanes H_i = {z_i(lambda) = 2}. For any union U of affine subspaces S_j of F3^r, E_i(1 - 1_U) = 1 - 1_{U'} with U' = cap_{a in F3} cup_j T_{j,a}, T_{j,a} = {mu : (mu, a) in S_j}. Each T_{j,a} is an affine subspace or empty. Proof: mu is bad iff every point (mu, a) of the fibre lies in some S_j. Distributing the intersection gives the union of T_{j0,0} cap T_{j1,1} cap T_{j2,2}, which are again affine subspaces. Subspaces with lambda_i-free equations (cylinders) pass through unchanged, which gives bucket locality. Hence SAT(F(G)) = (E_1 o ... o E_r)(Q_G) is computed without any 3^r normal form, as a sequence of unions of affine subspaces (RREF over F3, pruning by inclusion). SAT iff the final union is empty. (3) Machine check, scratchpad/aelim/ae.py and ae_exp.py: 0/200 mismatches against brute force on random 3-colouring instances (n 3..7), and 0/178 on the owner route (positive 1-in-3 SAT -> A z = 1 -> z = z0 + B lambda -> hyperplanes), r <= 9. (4) Cost is exactly the number of subspaces kept. It is bounded below by the affine cover number c(B_t) of the projected bad sets B_t, the partial assignments with no satisfying extension. c(B_t) is a semantic invariant independent of the representation and is the exact place where the method would fail. Measured peaks (4 seeds each; small sizes only, no asymptotic conclusion): random 1-in-3 at m = 0.62N, N = 15..60, peak N up to 3.4N; random 3-colouring at m = 2.3n, n = 8..18, peak <= 8.7n. Random 1-in-3 is believed easy (from memory, unverified), so it is not evidence of hardness or of ease. (5) Algebraic gain over plain variable elimination: subspaces such as {lambda_y = lambda_x + 1, lambda_z = lambda_x + 2} represent all-distinct colour patterns with codimension 2 instead of 6 codimension-3 points; for k = 3 this gives c = 2 instead of 6. OPEN, and the next step: a family where c(B_t) is superpolynomial for every elimination order (exact cause), or a class with polynomial c(B_t) beyond bounded treewidth (constructive gain). No lower-bound premise; no obligation closed.

structure.conclusion: E_i preserves unions of affine subspaces over F3; SAT = emptiness after r projections; cost = cover numbers c(B_t)

E(x)=E(y) forces each such value into [-2tau,2tau]; Parseval gives N d_H(x,y)=sum_u(...)^2 <= N 4tau^2, so d_H(x,y) <= 4tau^2. structure.conclusion: MIS GENERATORS OF THE KEMPE SPACE (owner 2026-11-27; PI check mis_span_check.py: 255 random graphs n<=8, rank W = rank gens = rank union, 0 mismatches; CLAIMED, Claude family only). G 3-colourable; I_G = {I independent, G-I bipartite}; M_G = inclusion-maximal members (= maximal independent sets of G with bipartite complement); R_G = {v: exists M in M_G, v in M, M-v in I_G}. THEOREM: W_G = span_Q({3*1_M - 1 : M in M_G} u {e_v : v in R_G}). PROOF: (a) W_G = span{3*1_I - 1 : I in I_G}: every I in I_G is a colour class (2-colour G-I); for classes A,B,C of a colouring 3*1_A-1 = (1_A-1_B)+(1_A-1_C), each a sum of Kempe vectors b_K; conversely b_K = 1_{K cap A}-1_{K cap B} = 1_A - 1_{A'} with A' the class after the swap, = ((3*1_A-1)-(3*1_{A'}-1))/3. (b) For I in I_G extend to a maximal independent M; G-M is an induced subgraph of G-I, so M in M_G; for v in M-I, M-v contains I, so M-v in I_G and v in R_G; 3*1_I-1 = (3*1_M-1) - 3*sum_{v in M-I} e_v. (c) 3e_v = (3*1_M-1)-(3*1_{M-v}-1) for v in R_G. QED. ALGORITHM: enumerate maximal independent sets with polynomial delay and polynomial space (Tsukiyama et al. 1977, from memory, verify at source), at most 3^{n/3} (Moon-Moser 1965); test bipartiteness of G-M and of G-(M-v); keep an incremental Q-basis (<= n vectors, Bareiss). With one colouring from any M in M_G, aff(Sol01(F(G))) = x_chi + W_G (x) U (17497). Time O*(3^{n/3}) = O*(1.4423^n), polynomial space. STRENGTH: exponential upper bound only; same enumeration as Lawler's 1976 3-colouring algorithm (from memory, verify), here lifted to the span. Hull computation is NP-hard (17497 (2)), so no polynomial version is expected. No lower bound, no obligation closed, no P vs NP progress.

statement: AFFINE RIGIDITY OF COLOURING SETS AND OF THEIR PROJECTIONS (owner theorem 2026-11-27 checked, PI extensions; CLAIMED, Claude family; novelty not checked). Scope note: USCCL is exactly min_B mu(H_B) = mu(G K_2). No broader conservation statement for parsimonious transformations is recorded. (R1, owner) If x, x+v, x+2v are proper 3-colourings over F3 and ij is an edge, then (x_i - x_j) + t(v_i - v_j) != 0 for t in F3, which forces v_i = v_j. Hence v is constant on every connected component and 0 on components with a pinned vertex. Proof checked; correct. (R2, PI) Exact cover number: let D be the span of the indicator vectors of the unpinned components (dim c_free). Every affine A = x + W contained in S = Col3(G, pins) has W in D, and x + D is contained in S. So the cosets of D partition S, and each A lies in one coset. Therefore a(S) = |S| / 3^{c_free}. For the pinned prism graph H(G) (connected, R pinned), a(Col3^pin(H)) = |Col3(G)| = U_G(1) over N. This is the owner's statement. Validation: no lines in pinned Col(H) for edgeless3, P3, K3, C5 and the prism graph (scratchpad/prism/rigid.py). (R3, PI) Projection rigidity: for T a subset of V and P = pi_T(Col3(G)), every point of P is a proper colouring of G[T]. R1 applies verbatim to G[T], so every line direction in P is a per-component shift of G[T]. Projection therefore never creates new line directions, and a(P) >= |P| / 3^{c(G[T])}. Validation: exhaustive over all T for C5, prism, W5 and three random 7-vertex graphs (13 edges); 0 non-shift directions found (scratchpad/prism/projlines.py). Example: projecting pinned Col(H) onto V(G) leaves Col3(G) with |Col3(G)|/3 shift lines for connected G (P3: 4, C5: 10, prism: 4); for edgeless G it gives F3^n with a = 1. (R4, PI) Two representations: in the positive representation (union of affine subspaces equal to S), existence elimination is projection, so a(pi S) <= a(S), which never grows; but the starting size is a(S) = |S| / 3^{c_free}, i.e. counting level. The negative representation of 17910 (union of affine subspaces equal to the complement) starts with m hyperplanes, and only projection can make it grow. The rigidity theorem constrains the positive representation only. The measured growth in 17910/17911 concerns the complement cover number, to which R1-R3 make no direct statement. Relevance: edgeless G already gives a = 3^n with trivial decision, so R1-R4 carry no hardness. No consequence of P=NP is derived. No obligation closed.

structure.conclusion: a(Col3(G,pins)) = |Col3| / 3^{c_free}; projections create only component shifts; positive vs complement representation

structure.conclusion: SHIFT-LEMMA19 (owner derivation 2026-11-26 from Viola's proof behind CHMY Lemma 19, director check; CLAIMED; model DTIME1: one-way read-only input tape, two-way work tape, CHMY l.146). Checked: (1) each work-head move crosses exactly one boundary of exactly one shift class d, so sum_d C_d(x) <= t, E_d C_d <= t/B, Pr_d[C_d > R] <= eta for R = ceil(t/(B eta)). (2) For fixed d a crossing record alpha (time-ordered, all boundaries) with l <= R entries (direction, state with current input symbol, input position) determines the block index (start block from d, then +-1 per crossing); input positions are non-decreasing, so K <= sum_{l<=R} (2q')^l binom(N+l, l), log K = O(R log(2q'(1+N/R))). (3) P_{d,alpha} simulates the block visits block by block, reading the input intervals in the order given by alpha (unknown-order read-once), storing one block (B cells), the state and a pointer into alpha: log w = O(B + log t). (4) F = (1/B) sum_d sum_{|alpha|<=R} P_{d,alpha}; determinism gives at most one consistent accepting alpha per d, so F = M Pr_d[C_d <= R] and 0 <= M - F <= eta pointwise; |E_G M - E_U M| <= eta + K delta. QUANTITATIVE (director): with B = sqrt(t log N), constant eta and q: R = Theta(sqrt(t/log N)), log K = Theta(sqrt(t log N)), log w = Theta(sqrt(t log N)), against Viola/CHMY O(sqrt t log(tq)): a gain of a factor sqrt(log N), so mu >= 0.505 - o(1) remains at t = N^{1.01}. STRUCTURAL CONSEQUENCE: even with zero cost for the input positions, log K >= R >= t/(B eta) while log w >= B (one block content), so max(log w, log K) >= sqrt(t/eta): compressing positions and states can remove at most the log factor; a polynomial gain needs a decomposition that either does not store a whole block content (log w << B) or has far fewer crossings than t/B - i.e. a different decomposition, not a better encoding of the crossing record. Consistent with JOINT-CONTROL-FLOOR seq 17284 (floor log(wK) for term-generic analyses). Novelty not checked; not a gap closure.

statement:
Q-BD (T43 sec.5) symbolically: linearization theorem checked, and its limit proved. CLAIMED, Claude family; literature marked.
(L1, owner's theorem, checked) Use GF(2) gate algebra: NOT=1+x, XOR=x+y, AND=xy. Process the gates in topological order and keep every gate as an affine form on the current affine piece P. If an AND input a is non-constant on P, split P into {a=0} and {a=1}; this lowers dim P by 1, and the gate becomes the affine form 0 or b on the two parts. If a is constant on P, no split is needed. The pieces form a parity decision tree of depth <= min(n,m), so there are <= 2^min(n,m) disjoint leaves. On each leaf the output is affine, and SAT on a leaf is linear algebra. Total time O*(2^min(n,m)). This is folklore-type and its novelty is not claimed.
(L2, extension) A leaf may stop early when every remaining gate has degree <= 2 on it. Then SAT of a quadratic GF(2) form is decided in poly time by Dickson's theorem (from memory; classical). Call A2 the class of algorithms that cover F2^n with affine pieces, by any procedure, and keep every gate of C as an explicit polynomial of degree <= 2 on each piece. A2 contains L1, the hybrid/merging calculus of 17917/17919 in its gate-wise form, and the AND-to-linear rule.
(L3, barrier theorem, proof) Suppose D: F2^n -> F2 is non-constant on every affine subspace of dimension d (an affine disperser). Then (i) D is not affine on any affine subspace V with dim V >= d+1. Proof: if D|V = l + c with l linear, then D is constant on the coset V cap {l=const}, whose dimension is >= d. (ii) D does not have degree <= 2 on any affine subspace V with dim V >= 2d+2. Proof: by Dickson normal form, a quadratic form on V of dimension k is affine on an affine subspace of dimension >= ceil(k/2) (fix one variable of each hyperbolic pair); then apply (i). Hence every A2 cover of a circuit containing a gate that computes D has >= 2^(n-2d-2) pieces. With C = D AND NOT D (unsatisfiable), no early exit through a satisfying leaf is possible. Consequence: if there is a poly-time computable D with d = O(log n), then every A2 algorithm needs time >= 2^n/poly(n) on some poly-size circuits. The n^{omega(1)} saving required by Williams/Q-BD is then impossible inside A2.
(Literature, from memory and search, to verify at the source) Li, ECCC TR23-023 (FOCS 2023): explicit affine extractors for entropy O(log n) with constant error. If that error is < 1/2, this gives the needed disperser with d = O(log n). Li 2015 (entropy polylog n) is not enough: it only gives the bound 2^(n - polylog n), which does not exclude a superpolynomial saving. That parity decision trees of affine dispersers have depth >= n - d is likely known (folklore). L3 is therefore expected to be known in substance; novelty is not claimed.
(Transfer to phi_C) A 1-in-3 clause is x+y+z=1 (affine) together with xy=yz=xz=0 (quadratic). The affine part therefore costs nothing (Gauss/hybrid). All the hardness lies in the quadratic constraints, so it is the same class A2 again. The exact transfer of L3 to Lemma-B images is not proved separately.
(Status) Not a lower-bound premise. It is an unconditional statement about an algorithm class: given the construction from the literature, it is a theorem. Linearization, Dickson leaves and gate-wise merging cannot by themselves give the Q-BD saving. Any Q-BD saving must contain a step outside A2. There are only two options: (a) the pieces are not affine, so they are varieties or sumsets; or (b) pieces are certified to be zero without making the gates explicit on them, which is global cancellation such as D AND NOT D = 0. Option (b) is the merging/normal-form problem of 17917 (Lemma G) and 17925, so it is not cheaper. Even a solved Q-BD gives only NEXP not in P/poly, not P != NP, and holds under P=NP as well (owner).

structure.conclusion: Q-BD: pure affine/quadratic linearization class A2 cannot yield the n^{omega(1)} saving (given explicit O(log n) affine dispersers, Li 2023, to verify at the source); a saving needs a step outside A2

(L3, barrier theorem, proof) Suppose D: F2^n -> F2 is non-constant on every affine subspace of dimension d (an affine disperser). Then (i) D is not affine on any affine subspace V with dim V >= d+1. Proof: if D|V = l + c with l linear, then D is constant on the coset V cap {l=const}, whose dimension is >= d. (ii) D does not have degree <= 2 on any affine subspace V with dim V >= 2d+2. Proof: by Dickson normal form, a quadratic form on V of dimension k is affine on an affine subspace of dimension >= ceil(k/2) (fix one variable of each hyperbolic pair); then apply (i). Hence every A2 cover of a circuit containing a gate that computes D has >= 2^(n-2d-2) pieces. With C = D AND NOT D (unsatisfiable), no early exit through a satisfying leaf is possible. Consequence: if there is a poly-time computable D with d = O(log n), then every A2 algorithm needs time >= 2^n/poly(n) on some poly-size circuits. The n^{omega(1)} saving required by Williams/Q-BD is then impossible inside A2.
(Literature, from memory and search, to verify at the source) Li, ECCC TR23-023 (FOCS 2023): explicit affine extractors for entropy O(log n) with constant error. If that error is < 1/2, this gives the needed disperser with d = O(log n). Li 2015 (entropy polylog n) is not enough: it only gives the bound 2^(n - polylog n), which does not exclude a superpolynomial saving. That parity decision trees of affine dispersers have depth >= n - d is likely known (folklore). L3 is therefore expected to be known in substance; novelty is not claimed.
(Transfer to phi_C) A 1-in-3 clause is x+y+z=1 (affine) together with xy=yz=xz=0 (quadratic). The affine part therefore costs nothing (Gauss/hybrid). All the hardness lies in the quadratic constraints, so it is the same class A2 again. The exact transfer of L3 to Lemma-B images is not proved separately.
(Status) Not a lower-bound premise. It is an unconditional statement about an algorithm class: given the construction from the literature, it is a theorem. Linearization, Dickson leaves and gate-wise merging cannot by themselves give the Q-BD saving. Any Q-BD saving must contain a step outside A2. There are only two options: (a) the pieces are not affine, so they are varieties or sumsets; or (b) pieces are certified to be zero without making the gates explicit on them, which is global cancellation such as D AND NOT D = 0. Option (b) is the merging/normal-form problem of 17917 (Lemma G) and 17925, so it is not cheaper. Even a solved Q-BD gives only NEXP not in P/poly, not P != NP, and holds under P=NP as well (owner).

statement: SUPPLEMENT TO 17922: TREEWIDTH OF G[K_t] AND THE COORDINATE CHANGE s = p+q (owner proofs 2026-11-27; PI check; CLAIMED, Claude family). (1) Theorem: tw(G[K_t]) = t(tw(G)+1) - 1, and the same for pathwidth, for every graph G and t >= 1. Upper bound: replace every vertex in each bag by its t copies. Lower bound: from a decomposition (T, B_x) of G[K_t] put B'_x = {v : all t copies of v in B_x}. Every v is covered: its copies form a clique, and by the Helly property of subtrees some bag contains the whole clique. Connectivity holds because an intersection of subtrees (subpaths) is a subtree (subpath). Every edge uv is covered: the 2t copies form a clique. Since |B'_x| <= |B_x|/t, we get tw(G)+1 <= floor((tw(G[K_t])+1)/t). Proof checked; correct. This replaces the 'from memory, unverified' formula in 17922. Pinned R: tw(H_rest) = 2 tw(G) + 1; free delta: 2 tw(G) + 2. (2) Coordinate change (owner): s_v = p_v + q_v, h_v = p_v, invertible. With R pinned the local constraints become h != 0, s - h != 0, 2h - s != 1, and the edges become s_u != s_w. Allowed local pairs (s,h): (0,1), (1,2), (2,1), exactly one h per s (scratchpad/aelim/coord.py). The decoded set x = -1 - s equals Col3(G) on 150 random graphs (0 mismatches). Primal graph J = G on the s-vertices plus one pendant h_v per vertex, so tw(J) = max(tw(G), 1), pathwidth likewise. (3) PI addition: since every s has exactly one h, eliminating h_v is free (exists h is always true). What remains is exactly G with colours relabelled by x = -1 - s. So the composition prism transformation -> linearization -> block encoding -> coordinate change -> local elimination is an exact round trip back to 3-colouring of G. The width 2 tw(G) + 1 of the block form is an artefact of the (p,q) coordinates. A linear change of coordinates removes it, but it never goes below tw(G). (4) USCCL consistency: USCCL (17585) concerns surjective parametrizations of the kernel K_G(A), 2 parameters per vertex, with min over B of mu(H_B) = mu(G K_2). J is a constraint representation of the solution set with 1 colour coordinate per vertex, a different object, so there is no contradiction. Status table: kernel overlap (USCCL, minimal) G K_2 with tw 2 tw(G)+1; prism block encoding 2 tw(G)+1 (pinned) / 2 tw(G)+2 (free delta); transformed constraint form max(tw(G), 1). No running-time improvement over G itself and no lower bound follow. No obligation closed.

structure.conclusion: ALG-COMP (owner derivation, director check). For C_a = circuits of size <= a: Z_{I u J}=Z_I n Z_J; P_I(C)=prod_{i in I}(1-(C(i)-x_i)^2) with P_{I u J}=P_I P_J; MCSP_a(x)=1 iff sum_C P_N(C) > 0 (a 2^{Theta(a log a)}-term count: REFORMULATION, not a reduction; small-characteristic evaluation invalid). D_I(C)=sum_{i in I}|C(i)-x_i| is additive; CC(x) <= CC(y)+c(m+1)d_H(x,y) (one minterm on m bits per changed position); with a=N^beta/(10m), b=N^beta: YES => D*=0, NO => D* > tau=(b-a)/(c(m+1))=Theta(N^beta/m); additive per-node errors with sum_v e_v < tau/2 suffice (sufficient, not necessary). DIMENSION: the indicators {P_I^x} have pairwise disjoint supports, hence are linearly independent; a single dyadic block of q positions suffices with q=Theta(a log a), because a pattern on q=2^h positions is a function of h index bits (Lupanov O(q/log q + m) gates). CORRECTION of the 2026-11-26 review note: 'mux needs 2^q <= a' confuses positions with input variables; its multi-block rescue fails as stated (one circuit must match all r blocks at once). The dimension bound excludes only fixed low-dimensional LINEAR representations and is superseded by FOURIER-SUP.

QO1 UPPER BOUND UNDER NP in P/poly (derivation of the OPS21 Thm 1.4 mechanism, author Claude family): NP subset SIZE[n^a] => there is K=K(a) such that for EVERY s=s(n) with n <= s <= 2^{n/2}: Gap-MCSP[s/(cn), s] on N=2^n bits has circuits of size N*s^K (a.e.). Proof: s'=s/(cn). Greedy anti-checker: V_0 = all circuits of size <= s', Y_0 = empty. Step i: for every position y in [N] (a fixed wire x_y) evaluate an approximate count of |{C in V_i: C(y) != x_y}|/|V_i| given (Y_i, x|Y_i, y, x_y) - input length L = O(t n), Stockmeyer approximate counting is in BPP^NP subset Sigma_3 subset P/poly (Karp-Lipton chain) so size L^{a'}; a tournament over the N candidates picks the best (y, x_y): N*L^{a'} gates per step. Elimination: if CC(x) > s then for every nonempty V_i some y kills >= 1/3 of V_i (minimax on V_i: otherwise a distribution over V_i is correct w.p. > 2/3 on every input and the majority of O(n) samples computes x with size O(n s') <= s, contradiction); with approximation >= 1/4. Hence V_t = empty after t = O(s' log s') steps. YES (CC(x) <= s'): the circuit for x is never eliminated. Final test 'V_t empty' is coNP on L bits. Total t*N*L^{a'} = N*s^{K}, K = a'+2, independent of s and beta. With s = N^beta: g_beta(N) <= N^{1+K beta} for all beta in (0,1/2]. c is the constant from the majority step (not necessarily 10).

statement: PRISM FACTORIZATION OF THE UNIVERSAL FUNCTION (contract 'Universal Prism Transformation', par. 3; CLAIMED, Claude family, no cross-family review). Definitions: U_G(X) = sum_{c in Col3(G)} prod_v X_{v,c(v)}. For H = H(G) (17911), U_H(X,Y,Z) uses X on the copies of V(G), Y_{i,j} = [colour of R_i is j] on the reference triangle, and Z on the gadget vertices. Statement: for every finite graph G, U_H(X,Y,1) = U_G(X) * perm(Y) with perm(Y) = sum_{pi in S3} prod_i Y_{i,pi(i)}. Moreover U_G(X) = coefficient of Y00 Y11 Y22 = U_H(X, I, 1). Proof: a proper colouring of H gives the triangle R a bijection pi. For fixed pi and fixed c in Col3(G), the gadget extension exists and is unique (17911 (a)). Hence the restriction to V(G) gives a bijection from the fibre over pi onto Col3(G). The sets are equal, and pi-invariance of Col3(G) is not needed for that. Summing over pi with Z = 1 gives the product. Setting Y = I kills every pi except the identity. Assumption: G is attached to R only through the gadgets. If vertices of G are pinned to R, the fibres become pi-dependent. Example: pinned path P3, Col not invariant under S3, checked. Validation: fibres over all 6 pi equal Col3(G) with multiplicity 1 for K3, P3, C5, C4+chord and the triangular prism; K4 gives 0 = 0 (scratchpad/prism/uh.py). Char 3: perm(J) = 6, so U_H(X,1,1) = 6 U_G = 0 in char 2 and 3. The full count vanishes, while the coefficient extraction Y = I is exact in every characteristic. Complexity consequence: U_G = U_H(X,I,1) and U_H(X,Y,1) = U_G * perm_3(Y) (a constant-size factor) are mutual p-projections. The prism transformation is therefore a p-equivalence of the universal functions. It neither gains nor loses algebraic complexity; this matches the contract warning that kernel preservation is not complexity preservation. The lattice index [L_H:M_H] = 3^r (17911) is a property of the colouring set, not of the circuit complexity of U_H. No obligation closed.

structure.conclusion: U_H(X,Y,1) = U_G(X) perm(Y); U_G = U_H(X,I,1); prism map is a p-equivalence

statement:
T52 (theory/T52-functional-qe-degree-reduction-2026-11-27.md): the owner's functional QE theorem over F3, with PI check, correction and composition analysis. CLAIMED.
Thm (owner, checked): 1-in-3 = affine F3 system plus Boolean domain (T41 Thm T); Gauss gives y_i = a_i(x) + l_i(z), z in F3^d. CORRECTION (PI): Q must cover ALL internal variables, including the free z_j, otherwise z_j=2 adds solutions and uniqueness fails. Q = prod_{i<=m}(y_i-2), F(x) = sum_z Q. (a) For a functional encoding, F(x) = +-1 if an extension exists, else 0. (b) deg F <= m-2d, because sum_t t^k = -1 for even k>0 and 0 otherwise, so every summed z_j uses at least 2 degrees. This is a Chevalley-Warning-type computation (row 1895); distinct from rows 2199/2200 (Ax-Katz on the slice never applies); novelty against the literature unchecked.
Prop 2.1: the excess e = m-2d is additive under substitution composition (d = d1+d2 with no new equations; m = m1+m2).
Prop 3.1: e >= wdeg_3(C) (weak/nonzero F3 degree); if C is satisfiable it has a satisfying input of weight <= e (minimal monomial plus Moebius). Example (proved): AND_n has e >= n. So the excess is a function invariant bounded below by the weak degree, not a new structure measure; no transformation removes it.
Efficiency: if e <= D, the coefficients come from F(1_T) with |T| <= D (unique propagation) in n^{O(D)} poly, with no sum over z. In general e can be Theta(n).
Relation to T51 T-D: the excess is additive and poly-bounded, but composition is F1(x)*F2(u(x)) (substitution, not a product of children); the degree comes from summation, not multiplication, so it gives no VSBR balanced product decomposition (E2 stays open). Contradiction test: all statements are unconditional; P=NP is not used; they are representation statements; no contradiction. First failing implication: 'low excess for general poly-size circuits' is false (AND_n).

structure.conclusion: Functional QE degree bound deg F <= m-2d verified (with all internal vars in Q); excess additive; excess >= weak F3 degree; no product structure for E2; no contradiction

MMW-M (CLAIMED; owner question 2026-11-26: does the MMW Merge architecture give the MECH-RANGE bound m <= N^{1-eps+4beta-7eta}?): in MMW19 Lemma 3.1 circuits the top tree has fan-out 1 (seq 9992), so every reused gate is (a) an output bit of a non-root Circuit-Min-Merge gate read more than once by the parent gate's replacement, or (b) a reused gate inside a replacement. There are >= N/l non-root gates (l-bit inputs cover N truth-table bits) with ~ s log s output bits each. MECH-RANGE then requires (a) l >= N^{eps-3beta+7eta} unless most description bits are read once by the parent, and (b) total reuse inside all replacements <= N^{1-eps+4beta-7eta}, i.e. per gate <= l N^{4beta-eps+o(1)}: for eps/beta -> infinity the gate function Circuit-Min-Merge[s] on l = N^{Omega(eps)} bits must be computed by near-formulas whose reuse is sublinear in l by a factor N^{-(eps-4beta)}. NP subset P/poly supplies arbitrary circuits for the gates and no such structure. So the architecture moves the whole m-bound into the gate function: the same reuse obligation (R-MCSP type) at scale l, as in MMW-UNFOLD (seq 17162). This is a NECESSARY condition derived from the architecture, not a proof that suitable gate circuits do not exist.

structure.conclusion: SEP-ELIM-LB (director, 2026-11-26; CLAIMED; generalises D2/T07). (a) Owner's recursive separator elimination: for a De Morgan circuit C (S gates, gamma reused gates) and a rooted decomposition of the reuse-variable dependency graph with separator sets Z_v such that every principal-formula consistency condition [z_i <-> P_i(x,z)] is placed at a node whose ancestors (inclusive) carry all z it mentions, H_v = OR_sigma (R_v^sigma AND AND_children H_u^sigma) computes C and L(C) <= sum_v w_v 2^{sum_{u<=v}|Z_u|} <= (S+gamma) 2^{W_path}. Correct; standard tree-decomposition-to-formula construction; one node holding all gamma reused gates gives T07 (seq 16758). (b) UNCONDITIONAL (from (a) + CJW20-GAP seq 17198): every De Morgan circuit of size S for Gap-MCSP[N^beta/(10 log N), N^beta] has W_path >= (2+beta-xi) log2 N - log2(S+gamma) - O(1) for EVERY such decomposition; for S = N^{1+K beta}: W_path >= (1-(K-1)beta-xi) log2 N - O(1). This is the separator form of COV1 class K1 (seq 16799), with r replaced by W_path. (c) LOGICAL STRENGTH of the owner's hypothesis H-sep ('under NP subset P/poly some QO1/MMW/OPS circuit of size N^{1+K beta} has W_path <= (1-delta) log2 N'): by (b) it is false for every circuit that exists unconditionally, and under QO1 it implies NP not subset P/poly directly; it is a reformulation of CONV-D with d(beta) = delta, not a reduction. Any separator analysis of the MMW/OPS architecture that does not use the internals of the hypothesis-supplied oracle circuits is therefore excluded. (d) Book search (reviewer item 1): no treewidth/separator analysis of MMW or OPS in the book; separator rows 60, 61, 9481, 3600-3659 concern other questions. Reviewer item 2 is answered by (b) quantitatively (about log N) and by SEP-MERGE-LB (witness-length scale) for block-faithful architectures.

CJ3-R (REPAIR of seq 16802 / Q-88090df9cf:S0139; owner construction 2026-11-26, director check; CLAIMED). Input x then y (n bits each), n known. m=ceil(log2(2n+2)), h=floor(log2 m), budget B=m^{max(1,floor(sqrt h))}. A* runs all programs of description length <= h (K <= 2m) as bit generators P(n,i), each cut off after B simulated steps; per program an active bit and a bit d_P. Every stream bit is compared with P(n,i) (mismatch or timeout deactivates); in the second half A* recomputes P(n,i) for x_i from the program instead of re-reading it and sets d_P |= P(n,i) AND y_i. Output: NOT d_P for an active program, else a fixed default b0. ONE PASS, no random access (objection 3 fixed); m(n) and the time bound are explicit (objections 1, 2 fixed). Correctness: a program still active at the end reproduced every input bit, so d_P = [x and y intersect]. T = n m^{O(sqrt log m)}, S = m^{O(sqrt log m)}, inside the CJSW class for f(n)=ceil(log2 log2(n+2)) (any f=omega(sqrt log log n)). Every fixed deterministic generator with (log n)^c time per bit is enumerated and within budget for all large n, so A* answers correctly on its outputs. COLLISIONS: if u != v are prefixes produced by such generators, the generator of u is active after u and inactive after v, so A*'s states differ (for all large n): deterministic polylog-time collision generators are EXCLUDED against A* (unconditional). Under P=NP the PH collapses on input length m=log n, so every polylogtime-uniform AC0 generator (single bit in PH on m) is computed in time m^{O(1)}=(log n)^{O(1)} and is also captured.
Lemma O1-B: if a poly-time algorithm maps every bipartite G to a skew-symmetric integer matrix B(G) with Pf(B(G))=#PM(G), then FP=#P (so P=P^#P, PH collapses).
structure.justification: Pfaffian of an integer skew matrix is exactly poly-time (Mahajan-Subramanya-Vinay fraction-free, value+sign); compose with the poly-time construction to get #PM in FP; #PM bipartite = 0/1-permanent = #P-complete (Valiant). Reviewed VALID.

structure.conclusion: CJ4 W-D IS A CHARACTERISATION OF O*, NOT AN INDEPENDENT ROUTE: against the P=NP algorithm A_PNP (CJ1) two simple prefixes u != v with a simple distinguishing suffix never collide, because A_PNP is correct on all simple inputs. So 'uniform collisions for every admissible A' includes refuting the streaming compressor of route M on simple strings - the O* obligation (update-cost lower bound) in another form; information counting cannot do it (|simple prefixes| <= 2^{O(m^2 log m)}, O(m^2 log m) state bits suffice). Relation A/D/G: they share the 'structured selection' theme, but no transfer between A and D or between G and D is proved; G1's 'merges with D1c' is downgraded to 'related, transfer unproved'.

JOINT-CONTROL-FLOOR (director, 2026-11-26; extends CHMY-SEED-FLOOR seq 17279 to the owner's proposal 'control the error of the whole state distribution jointly instead of per branching program'; CLAIMED). (1) What is needed is only ONE-SIDED: if M decides MCSP[s] correctly, it accepts every string of CC <= s and Pr_U[M=1] <= gamma := Pr_U[CC <= s] <= 2^{O(s log s) - N}; a contradiction follows as soon as Pr_G[M=1] < 1, i.e. G is a hitting set for the complement of M (density >= 1 - gamma). This is weaker than the two-sided 1/6 condition. (2) FLOOR for every analysis that uses only the decomposition M = OR_{alpha in A} P_alpha with each P_alpha a read-once BP of width <= w (any fixed order per alpha) and Pr_U[M=1] <= gamma: let H be the image of G (all CC <= s, so |H| <= 2^{O(s log s)} and |H| 2^{-N} <= gamma). A width-w ROBP in any fixed order accepts any prescribed set of <= w strings (one path per string, <= w distinct prefixes per level), so H is the union of ceil(|H|/w) such ROBPs; if ceil(|H|/w) <= |A| this OR is a member of the class, has acceptance measure |H| 2^{-N} <= gamma, and accepts all of H. Hence the analysis can succeed only if |H| > w |A|, i.e. s log s >= Omega(log w + log |A|). This holds for joint, one-sided, distribution-level error control (S0258/S0290-type compression of state distributions included) as long as the pieces are treated as generic ROBPs. (3) For CHMY Lemma 19, log(w |A|) = Theta(sqrt t log tq), so again mu >= 0.505 - o(1) at t = N^{1.01}. MECHANISM EXCLUDED (on confirmation): joint/one-sided error control over the Lemma-19 family with generic pieces. REQUIRED for mu = o(1) at the generator level: either a decomposition of O(1)-state time-N^{1.01} one-tape DTMs with log(w |A|) = N^{o(1)}, or an analysis using properties of M beyond 'OR of |A| width-w ROBPs' (its O(1) states / uniformity; by seq 17279 (c) the guarantee must fail at 2^{poly(s)} states). The transfer of the OpenAI Lemma 3.2 functional to TM transition matrices is not proved. The route uses MMW (Theorem 47), so it is not independent of QE*.

CROSS-CHMY check (owner derivation 2026-11-26, director check; CLAIMED). (0) Sign: delta_ad delta_bc = delta_ac delta_bd - eps_ab eps_cd with eps_01 = 1, eps_10 = -1 is exactly the identity recorded in seq 17297 (1) (minus sign, verified on 16 points); no correction needed. (1) Embedding Delta = sum_alpha sum_x W(x) P_alpha(x), W = Pr_G - 2^{-N}: correct by linearity, over Q. (2) Unfolded-circuit tensor network M(x) = sum_z [z_out = 1] prod_g [z_g = g(z_in(g))]: correct (unique consistent assignment), standard circuit-to-tensor-network embedding; for a one-tape DTM the unfolded network is the space x time tableau, a planar local network, so it still contains no crossings for the identity of seq 17297 to act on (seq 17297 (2) unchanged). (3) Weighted Cauchy-Schwarz |Delta|^2 <= p chi^2, chi^2 = sum_{p_alpha>0} (g_alpha - p_alpha)^2 / p_alpha (p_alpha = 0 forces g_alpha = 0 since P_alpha then accepts nothing): correct, BUT DOMINATED: by the same Cauchy-Schwarz, sum_alpha |g_alpha - p_alpha| <= sqrt(p chi^2), so |Delta| <= sum_alpha |g_alpha - p_alpha| <= sqrt(p chi^2); the weighted balance is never stronger than the triangle inequality, which itself contains no factor |A|. In CHMY |A| enters only through the UNIFORM per-term error eps' = eps/|A| (Cor 39), not through the triangle inequality; the weighted form removes nothing. (4) LOGICAL STRENGTH of CROSS-RES (chi^2 < 1/(36p)): it implies sum_alpha |g_alpha - p_alpha| < 1/6, the old obligation, so it is at least as hard; term-generic bounds are covered by JOINT-CONTROL-FLOOR seq 17284. If M is a correct MCSP[s] algorithm and G is supported in {CC <= s}, then Delta = 1 - p and chi^2 >= (1-p)^2/p > 1/(36p); so CROSS-RES for such G is equivalent to M not being a correct MCSP algorithm - a reformulation of the lower bound, not a reduction. STATUS: CROSS-ID, embedding and the weighted inequality are correct and standard; they do not shrink the gap. The open step remains a non-uniform, resource-using per-term error estimate (seq 17279, 17284, 17286, 17297).

structure.conclusion: ROBUST-GAMMA (owner derivation 2026-11-26, director check; CLAIMED, corollary of the CJW20 Thm 5.5 proof). a = N^beta/(10 log N), tau = N^gamma, 0 < beta < gamma < 1. Promise: YES = some a-circuit at distance 0, NO = every a-circuit at distance > tau. Restriction with k >= N^{gamma+o(1)} free bits (p = N^{gamma-1+o(1)}): Pr[some a-circuit within tau] <= 2^{O(N^beta)} 2^{tau log(ek/tau)} 2^{-k} = 2^{-Omega(k)}; restricted size p^2 L N^{o(1)}, CKLM PRG outputs have size L_rest^{1/3+o(1)} <= a iff L <= N^{2+3beta-2gamma-xi}. So the promise problem has no probabilistic De Morgan formulas of size N^{2+3beta-2gamma-xi}. SAMPLING (checked): t = O(N^{1+beta-gamma}) uniform positions J; NO: each a-circuit survives with prob <= e^{-t tau/N}, union over 2^{O(N^beta)} circuits; YES always accepted. So a uniform bound L(H_{J,a}) <= L_H for the partial-consistency predicate H_{J,a} gives probabilistic formulas of size L_H (J hard-wired). In t: N^{2+3beta-2gamma} = t^{2+beta/u}, u = 1+beta-gamma, which is CJW20's exponent 2+theta for MCSP[t^theta] with theta = beta/u (consistency check: no new strength).

If every nonzero entry A[u,v] of a Gal matrix has |v \ u| = 1, the Gal ratio is at most k = C(n,3): each such entry lies in exactly one clause rectangle R_j, so A = sum_j A|R_j with disjoint supports and rank(A) <= sum_j rank(A|R_j) <= k * max_j rank(A|R_j). Any improvement over k must use entries with |v \ u| >= 2.

PARITY TEST T-NORM (CONDITIONAL on lemma CORR): a normalization valid for all functions is impossible, so NORM must use a property of Gap-MCSP that parity lacks. Argument: parity has linear-size circuits; if it had a circuit of size <= N^{1+eps} with W <= N^{beta-2eta}, then under the p-restriction (p = N^{beta+eps/5-1}) w.p. >= 1 - N^{-eta} the restricted circuit has gamma <= N^{beta-eta} reused gates, and by D4 some formula of size s ~ p^2 N^{1+eps} = N^{2beta-1+7eps/5} has correlation >= 2^{-N^{beta-eta}} with parity on k = pN = N^{beta+eps/5} live variables; k^2/s = N^{1-eps}. CORR (source not yet checked): De Morgan formulas of size s have correlation <= exp(-(k^2/s)^c) with PARITY_k for a constant c > 0. If c(1-eps) > beta - eta, contradiction. Use: every proposed normalization must fail on the linear parity circuit.

structure.conclusion: DYNAMIC-CUT + DYNAMIC-CUT-AMORTIZED + FAMILY-CHECKER-CEILING (owner derivations 2026-11-26, director check; CLAIMED). VERIFIED BY AUTHOR: (1) DYNAMIC-CUT: in an input-free phase, H(R^1 | R^0, C_c) = 0 (each side evolves from its own content and the crossing states), so H(R^1|R^0), H(L^1|L^0) <= H(C_c) = O(E m_c + 1) for O(1) states, and E T >= Omega(F) - O(|cuts|). Transposition r x r on one tape: F = (r-1) r (r^2-1)/3, T = Omega(b^2). (2) Two-phase check (tape holds y row-major and nothing else, then z is read column-major, accept iff z = y^T): combining the left half of one accepting run with the right half of another with the same crossing protocol (incl. input positions) gives an accepting run on a mixed input, so the left-stored bits read on the right are a function of C; from b = H(Y) <= H(C) + E[b - |S(C)|] follows E|S| <= H(C), both directions E D_c <= 2 H(C_c), H(C_c) = O((E m_c + 1) log b); for every cut in the middle half every column has >= r/4 - O(1) bits on each side, so E m_c = Omega(r) and E T = Omega(b^{3/2}). Section 6 (false acceptances, + 2 lambda) not checked in detail. (3) DYNAMIC-CUT-AMORTIZED: with the same protocol, every left alternative combines with every right alternative to an admissible window alternative, D_j >= a^L a^R, E log a^L >= H(Y_{J^L} | L^0, L^1, C) (injectivity of pi_j; log of the class value count >= conditional entropy), so sum_j (E^L_j + E^R_j) <= Lambda - b. Type: classical crossing-sequence / information-flow arguments (Hennie-type); novelty not checked. STRENGTH (director): the deficits condition on whole half-tape contents; a machine that writes every read input bit onto the tape (O(1) per bit) has L^1, R^1 containing the read bits, so E^L = E^R = 0 for every window and cut. The amortized balance is therefore satisfied at linear cost and yields no time bound by itself; only the flux bound (1) with a forced storage layout gives time, and in the one-way-input model the layout is chosen by the machine (two orders prepared once, 17325). FAMILY-CHECKER-CEILING (director, generalises the exclusion of seq 17325): let F = {x(y)} with x(y)_i = y_{a(i)} for an explicit address map a computable by a size-<=s circuit (every construction used so far: Lupanov addressing seq 17314, permuted repetitions seq 17325, grids). The machine M_F reads y, writes it and the address circuit on the tape, and for each i evaluates a(i) and walks to y_{a(i)}: DTIME1[N (b + poly(s))] = DTIME1[N poly(s)], deterministic, no oracle; it accepts exactly F, |F| = 2^b <= 2^Lambda, and rejects every hybrid. Hence every argument whose premises are 'M accepts F and accepts few inputs / few hybrids' plus machine structure (cut-and-paste, crossing protocols, static or dynamic information flow, any choice of cuts and permutations) proves at most t <= time(M_F) = N s^{c_F}. CHMY Thm 1 needs N^{1.01} for every mu > 0 (its footnote), and N s^{c_F} < N^{1.01} for mu < 0.01/c_F. MECHANISM EXCLUDED (on confirmation): explicit hard-input families with polynomially checkable decoders plus counting plus any cut-and-paste/information-flow analysis, as a route to the magnification hypothesis. A continuation must use acceptance of YES instances outside every such family, i.e. a family whose membership is itself not decidable in DTIME1[N^{1.01}], which is a lower bound of the same kind. PRECISION to seq 17318 (owner): the bound log(w'K') >= max(h, log K_acc) concerns the width budget w' = 2^h+1 and the count of that construction, not the width of every realised ROBP; the entropy bound K_acc >= 2^{H(alpha(X))} is unrestricted. Not a gap closure.

structure.conclusion: ANTHROPIC-CROSSING vs CHMY Lemma 19 (owner proposal 2026-11-26, director check; CLAIMED). Source: 'A 2^{o(n)} time algorithm for 3-SAT' (Claude/Anthropic), local since 2026-11-17 at literature/sources/anthropic-eth (paper.txt, Lean files); crossing decomposition l.164-176 and Section 2.5 l.474ff (2 [x=v][y=u] = row term + column term, eight-square identity for lambda = 3 bits, Appendix B for general lambda); runtime Theorem 1 l.55: 2^{O(min{k n loglog n / log n, k m / log m})}. (1) Owner identity [x=v][y=u] = [x=u][y=v] - phi(x,y) phi(u,v), phi(x,y) = [x != y](-1)^x, verified on all 16 points; it is the lambda = 1 (two-square) instance of the Anthropic decomposition; the correction for weights A, B is exactly -(A(0,1)-A(1,0))(B(0,1)-B(1,0)) and vanishes if one weight is symmetric. (2) STRUCTURE: the Lemma-19 sum M = sum_alpha P_alpha is a PATH (one-dimensional) contraction: each constraint is an equality of crossing sequences at ONE cut between ADJACENT blocks; no two constraints cross, so the crossing identity has nothing to act on unless the chain is first re-embedded; Anthropic's rewriting removes the cost of crossings (expansion), while a path network is already contracted at cost poly(bond dimension) - and the bond dimension w = exp(Theta(sqrt t log tq)) (crossing-sequence information) is exactly the CHMY bottleneck. structure.conclusion: QUANTIFIER Q-WILLIAMS (owner 2026-11-26): 'for every k there is L_k in NP with L_k not in SIZE(n^k)' does not imply P != NP: by Kannan 1982, Sigma2 cap Pi2 is not in SIZE(n^k) for every fixed k; under P = NP, PH = P, so already P contains such an L_k for every k. Needed is the uniform-quantifier form 'EXISTS L in NP FORALL k: L not in SIZE(n^k)' (NP not in P/poly), or the uniform analogue for DTIME. Fixed-polynomial NP lower bounds and NQP lower bounds (Murray-Williams) are not approximations of P != NP.

structure.conclusion: INTERVAL-LINEARISATION (owner 2026-11-27, director check; CLAIMED, needs review by another model family). Setting: full roABP-IPS refutation C(x,y) of Psi_n (axioms = clause products Q_j of literal indicators, placeholders y_j), width w in a total order pi of x and y; I_j = span in pi of {y_j} union vars(Q_j); N = placeholders occurring in a monomial with another placeholder or with degree >= 2; p_N = max over cuts of #{j in N : I_j crosses the cut} (p_N <= owner's p). CLAIM: Psi_n has an roABP-IPS_LIN refutation (functional form, Boolean-axiom terms free) of width <= 1 + m w 2^{p_N} in the induced x-order; with Theorem 12 (seq 5128): log2 w + p_N >= c1 n - O(log m), c1 = Theorem 12 exponent constant (not explicit). PROOF. (A) Telescoping: C(x,Q) - C(x,0) = sum_j [C(Q_<j,1,0_>j) - C(Q_<j,0,0_>j)] Q_j =: sum_j Q_j D_j pointwise on the cube, since Q_j in {0,1} there; so sum_j Q_j D_j = 1 on the cube. For j not in N, D_j = coefficient g_j(x) of y_j, width <= w (coefficient extraction, as Lemma 15 (i), seq 5174). For j in N only placeholders in N are substituted. (B) Cut rank: at a pi-cut write C = sum_{k<=w} A_k(x_L,y_L) B_k(x_R,y_R). For y_i on the left with I_i crossing, Q_i = L_i(x_L) R_i(x_R) (on the cube); Moebius expansion in the Boolean values gives A_k(x_L,Q) = sum_{T subset S_L} alpha_{k,T}(x_L) prod_{i in T} L_i prod_{i in T} R_i, each term rank 1; same for B_k. Non-crossing placeholders are one-sided functions (no cost). Hence cube-evaluation rank of D_j at the cut <= w 2^{p_N}. ml(D_j) has coefficient-matrix rank = cube-evaluation rank (Kronecker product of invertible 2x2 transforms, every field), so ml(D_j) is an roABP of width <= w 2^{p_N} in the induced order (Nisan). (C) sum_j Q_j ml(D_j) - 1 vanishes on the cube, hence lies in the Boolean ideal. Theorem 12 is functional: Lemma T (report l.268-274) uses only 'on the cube the Boolean-axiom terms vanish' and the cube rank of a_D at a cut, so the Boolean quotients h need no width bound. REVIEW POINT: check that Lemma O (order reduction, report l.323-346) is likewise only a restriction of the a_D (functional), so Theorem 12 applies to cube-rank widths. STRENGTH/REDUNDANCY: incomparable with Theorem 14 (placeholder degree <= c' n, seq 5169) and Lemma 15 (t placeholder monomials, seq 5174); covers part of the Theorem 14 remainder (degree > c' n with nonlinear placeholders spread so few cross any cut). Not covered: certificates with >= c1 n - log(mw) nonlinear placeholders crossing some cut; Theorem 16 (seq 5192) shows every order has a cut crossed by K = Omega(n) disjoint clauses, so the canonical product certificate has p_N = Omega(n) and the bound is vacuous there (Theorem 16 handles it). Whether c1 exceeds the minimal crossing density is not decided (c1 not explicit). Telescoping is routine (TR26-070 Sec. 7, local paper.txt l.727-753; Grochow-Pitassi Prop. 2.1); novelty of the 2^p substitution cost not checked in the literature. Restricted proof-system lower bound only; no consequence for P != NP; M9 remains open.

structure.conclusion: HYBRID-BUDGET + CUT-PASTE-LOCAL + GRID-LA, replacement of seq 17325 (owner derivation 2026-11-26, director check; CLAIMED). Model DTIME1 (one-way input, one work tape, alphabet Gamma). Family x(y): prefix y in {0,1}^b, then K = Theta(N/b) repetitions pi_j(y) at fixed input positions, every x(y) of CC <= s, |L_s| <= 2^Lambda, Lambda = O(s log s). VERIFIED BY AUTHOR: (i) sum_y |L_s(y)| <= 2^Lambda, so E_Y log|L_s(Y)| <= Lambda - b (Jensen). (ii) CUT-PASTE-LOCAL: windows = time intervals in which the input head is on segment j (reads of a segment belong to its window); sigma_j = (visited interval I_j, entry/exit contents of I_j, entry/exit control and head positions, duration). If sigma_j agrees, the full configuration at window exit is unchanged, so alternatives in different windows combine by induction even when the I_j overlap; distinct combinations give distinct inputs; prod_j D_j(y) <= |L_s(y)|. (iii) Since pi_j is injective and the window run depends only on (entry part of sigma_j, segment), every y' with sigma_j(y') = sigma_j(y) is an admissible alternative; E log D_j >= H(Y | sigma_j) = b - H(sigma_j), hence sum_j H(sigma_j) >= K b - (Lambda - b) and the average is >= b - O(N^{2mu-1} log N) for b = Theta(s), mu < 1/2. (iv) GRID-LA: b = r^2, row- and column-major orders; every injective arrangement has sum over grid edges of |pi(u)-pi(v)| = Omega(r^3) (each of the ~b/2 balanced cuts cuts Omega(r) edges; this is the classical Theta(r^3) minimum linear arrangement of the grid). In the single-copy static-storage model this gives t = Omega(N sqrt b). STRENGTH: H(sigma_j) <= 2|I_j| log|Gamma| + O(log tN), so (iii) gives only sum_j |I_j| >= Omega(N), no more than the reading time. EXCLUSION (director): let C = {x(y)} (consistent tables). The machine M_C that accepts exactly C satisfies every premise used ((i)-(iii) with L_s replaced by C, budget b - b = 0, the strongest case) and runs in DTIME1[O(N + b^2)]: store the prefix y, build a column-major copy once (O(b^2) naive), then check each repetition by one linear sweep against the copy of its order (O(b) per repetition). For b <= sqrt N (mu < 1/2) this is linear. Hence (1) the transfer of (iv) to arbitrary work-tape encodings is FALSE for this family (two copies beat the N sqrt b bound), and (2) MECHANISM EXCLUDED (on confirmation): a fixed repetition family plus counting of accepted hybrids plus cut-and-paste cannot give a superlinear bound for mu < 1/2. Any continuation must use the correctness of M on YES instances that M_C rejects. CORRECTED (owner 2026-11-26): independently chosen orders cost a description each, but a jointly generated family does not: x_y(a,z) = y(A_a z) with A_a = I + U_a unipotent upper-triangular over F_2 (bits of a in distinct entries above the diagonal, needs h(h-1)/2 >= n-h), b = 2^h, gives K = 2^{n-h} = Theta(N/s) distinct permutations with CC(x_y) <= O(h^2) + O(b) <= s. This family is still covered by the checker ceiling of seq 17328 (compute A_a z per address, fetch y: DTIME1[N (b + h^2)]). QUANTIFIER: Theorem 1 of CHMY needs MCSP[N^mu] not in DTIME1[N^{1.01}] for every mu > 0 (footnote: the exists-mu form is equivalent); a bound of the form t >= N s^c with fixed c fails for mu < 0.01/c, so t/N must not be bounded by any fixed power of s, while Corollary 17 gives DTIME1^O[N poly(s)] with poly(s)-length queries (Lemma 16: N O~(s^2) with a Sigma3 oracle). So the argument must fail for that oracle machine; there, query contents of length poly(s) >= b can carry the window information. SOURCE: the owner withdrew the citation of the preprint 'J. A. Wittcop, Nov 2026' on 2026-11-26 (not verifiable); the derivations above do not depend on it. Not a gap closure.

(1) VERIFIED BY AUTHOR: P = NP => PH = P => BPP = P (Sipser-Gacs-Lautemann) => PIT in P => IPS certificates are verifiable in P => the prefix predicate is in P and short IPS refutations are found bit by bit (length by doubling): P = NP => IPS proof search is automatable. This is seq 17136 (E-AUTOMATE, resolution) transferred to IPS. Only one direction is available for IPS ('automatable => P = NP' is Atserias-Mueller for resolution, not known for IPS), so 'IPS is not automatable' is a statement whose truth implies P != NP. 17136(b) applies verbatim: invariants of the certificates themselves (existence, size, annihilators, dual certificates, degree) are unconditional statements that also hold if P = NP, so they cannot bound findability against all algorithms; reductions of the Atserias-Mueller type give the converse direction (automatable => P = NP). BARRIER CHECK (promised for owner step 2): the transfer relativises (and algebrises), so a proof of non-automatability needs a non-relativising and non-algebrising step; no candidate step is named. MECHANISM EXCLUDED (extends 17136): invariant-based limits on IPS proof search as a route to P != NP. (2) CARRY-DICKSON, VERIFIED BY AUTHOR: XOR part solved by Gaussian elimination (x = x0 + By), carry equations become quadratics q_j; reducing modulo the span of their quadratic parts leaves r quadratic plus affine equations; Z = 2^{-r} sum_lambda sum_y (-1)^{lambda.q(y)}, each inner sum 0 or +-2^{e-k_lambda} by Dickson, computable in poly time; hence exact counting/decision in 2^r poly(|F|). statement: EXACT TRIANGLE AND PRISM LINEARIZATION IN THE HYBRID ELIMINATION (owner task 2026-11-27; PI proofs, implementation and measurements; CLAIMED, Claude family). (1) Rules, with proofs. Triangle: a, b, c pairwise distinct in F3 iff a+b+c = 0 and a != b (17911 (1)). Prism with top t, bottom b, rungs t_i b_i: all 9 edges hold iff the top triangle holds, b_i - t_i = d for i = 0,1,2, and d != 0. Proof: for fixed top bijection pi, the bottom bijection sigma must have no fixed point relative to pi. So sigma pi^{-1} is a 3-cycle of F3, i.e. a translation c -> c+d with d = 1 or 2. Count 6*2 = 12. (2) Implementation (scratchpad/aelim/linearize.py). The derived equations go into the hybrid E; all edge hyperplanes stay in U. hybrid.normalize reduces them modulo E. Edges equal up to sign modulo E collapse to one retained disequality; edges constant modulo E vanish. Soundness: every derived equation is implied by the original edges. Completeness: each dropped edge is implied by E plus its retained representative. Validation: solution sets {E} minus union U equal Col3 exactly on 200 random graphs with n <= 9, half with a planted prism (0 mismatches), and on all benchmark instances below. (3) Benchmark: same instances and orders as 17919 (G: order 0..n-1; H: gadgets first) (scratchpad/aelim/lin_bench.log). K3: H has 24 vars, 51 edges, 11 triangles, 6 prisms, rank E 17, free dim 7, 11 retained disequalities, |S| = |Col| = 36. P3: 24 vars, rank 16, free dim 8, 12 retained, 72 = 72. C5: 38 vars, 83 edges, 16 triangles, 10 prisms, rank 26, free dim 12, 21 retained, 180 = 180. Peak forbidden count over start and all stages: H 11, 12, 21 (before linearization 66, 65, 98); G 1, 2, 5 (the start count of retained edges). No stage exceeded the start count. Runtime C5-H 42.5 s against 362.7 s. (4) Structure (hand derivation, consistent with the counts). Let R0 + R1 + R2 = 0, a_v = R0 + dA_v, b_v = R1 + dB_v, v = -(a_v + b_v). Retained per vertex: dA != 0, dB != 0, dA - dB != R1 - R0. Exactly 3 pairs (dA, dB) remain, and their sums run through F3 once, so the gadget is a bijection onto the colour of v. Retained globally: R0 != R1 and one disequality s_u != s_w per edge of G (s = dA + dB); triangles of G collapse further (K3: 3 -> 1). Counts 3n + 1 + m: P3 12, C5 21; K3 9 + 1 + 1 = 11. Free dim = 2 + 2n - (rank of G's own triangle equations): 7, 8, 12. (5) Composition. Universal function: the linear part carries the factor perm(Y) (R with R0 != R1 = 6 points = S3) and the gadget bijections. The nonlinear residual is exactly G's edge set in the variables s_v. So the linearization realises 17913 / Fable A2 (U_H = U_G under monomial substitutions) at the level of the elimination representation: Prism(G) adds no nonlinear content beyond G. USCCL (17585; min_B mu(H_B) = mu(G K_2)): in the parameters (dA_v, dB_v) the edge constraints s_u != s_w have support {dA_u, dB_u, dA_w, dB_w}. The residual support hypergraph is therefore G[K_2] (each vertex blown up to its 2 parameters) plus within-block constraints and the global R parameters. This is the overlap pattern USCCL-NL forces, so the linearized representation meets the USCCL structure. Whether mu of the residual equals mu(G K_2) exactly, with the R parameters as apex, is not checked. No lower bound and no hardness reading of the counts; small sizes only. No obligation closed.

structure.conclusion: triangle/prism linearization exact; Prism(G) residual = G edges in s_v; peaks 66/65/98 -> 11/12/21

statement:
T48 (theory/T48-gate-algebra-simultaneous-linearization-cancellation-2026-11-27.md). CLAIMED, Claude family; cross-family review pending.
Thm1 (owner's simultaneous linearization) checked: min cover of a layer g_i=a_i b_i with all gates affine = 2^{r_*}, r_* = min dim span{l_i in {alpha_i,beta_i,alpha_i+beta_i}}. Lemma 1.1: ab is affine on p+W iff alpha|W, beta|W are dependent; the case alpha=beta uses the Boolean identity a^2=a. r_*<=k is an NP predicate; efficient computation is open.
Prop2.2: the polar-form characterization (B_Q|W=0) is exact only for deg<=2. For deg>=3 the condition depends on the coset (x1x2x3, W=<e1,e2>). Prop2.3: multiplicative depth 1 is solved in poly time by Dickson, so linearization pays off only from depth 2 onward.
Thm3 (cancellation dichotomy): formal zero test in coRP (Schwartz-Zippel over F_{2^{s+2}}); Boolean zero test (mod x^2+x) is coNP-complete; coefficient of x1...xn in NF(C) = parity of #SAT, so the exact normal form is ParityP-hard; deg NF(C|P)<=k is coNP-hard (C*y1..y_{k+1}). Direct output analysis = Boolean ideal membership on pieces = Q-BD itself.
Thm4 (limit of A2): Li ECCC TR23-023 Thm1.7, VERIFIED AT THE SOURCE: for every constant eps there is an explicit affine extractor for entropy >= c log n; eps=1/4 gives an affine disperser with d=c log n. This closes the literature item of 17938. For C_n = E AND NOT E (unsatisfiable, poly size), every A2 algorithm (affine pieces, every gate of degree <=2, any adaptive/simultaneous/merging cover) needs >= 2^{n-2c log n-1} pieces. Hybrid pieces A minus union of B_j are open. This is a statement about an algorithm class, not a general lower bound; it is consistent with P=NP.
Prop5.1: Q-BD with propagation-complete backdoor <=> Circuit-SAT in 2^n/n^{omega(1)} poly(s) for poly-size circuits (Williams' hypothesis); direction <= by a unit-propagation circuit. Q-BD is therefore not an easier intermediate problem.
Prop5.2: P=NP => NEXP not in P/poly (Sigma2=P; Meyer/Karp-Lipton: EXP in P/poly => EXP=Sigma2; time hierarchy; classical, from memory). So the Williams route can never supply the contradicting consequence K.
Sec6: under P=NP the gate algebra yields only relativizing NP-predicate consequences (r_*, minimal covers, Boolean membership), which hold in the AW world (17590). The chain 'Thm4 + simulation of all poly-time algorithms in A2' has a premise S that is equivalent to P!=NP (vacuous if P!=NP), so it is an equivalent formulation and a forbidden transfer, not a route.
Open: (Q-BD) a saving mechanism for Boolean ideal membership outside A2 and outside formal identity (= Williams' hypothesis); (P!=NP) unchanged from 17920/17929: a consequence K of P=NP with a non-relativizing step whose negation is proved unconditionally. P!=NP has not been proved.

structure.conclusion: Simultaneous linearization verified; cancellation dichotomy (formal coRP / Boolean coNP / NF ParityP-hard); A2 limit unconditional via Li 2023 (verified); Q-BD <=> Williams' hypothesis; Williams route cannot supply K; first unproved implication unchanged

statement:
T53 (theory/T53-formal-semantic-existential-qe-2026-11-27.md). CLAIMED.
Sec.1 (owner's construction, PI checked each step): complement pairs (y-2)(ybar-2) = -(y+1)^2 = -1 on {0,1}, 0 at 2; coupling E(x,xbar,0), E(x,ubar,a), E(xbar,u,b) gives a=u-x, b=x-u, both Boolean <=> u=x, so the encoding stays functional; (a-2)(b-2) = 1-(x-u)^2. With u free, formally F_C(X) = eps prod(-1-X_i) sum_{u:C(u)=1} prod(1-(X_i-u_i)^2). The degree-h homogeneous part is +-HC_h. Equivalence (nonuniform, F3): all formal QE polynomials of poly functional encodings in VP <=> VP=VNP (=> Strassen homogenization plus HC VNP-complete; <= ternary parameter as two bits with factor (1-b1 b2)). On Boolean X, F_C = +-prod(-1-X)C(X) is poly-time; the VNP hardness lies entirely in the Boolean-ideal component.
Sec.2: formal QE (linear in values), semantic projection (fibre/count), existential QE (OR). Functional case: existential = formal mod the Boolean ideal. General case: counting mod 3. Prop E1 (proved): OR_{2^d} has unique multilinear degree 2^d, so existence has value-degree 2^d versus 1 for sums (with C1: linear only in idempotent semirings).
Sec.3 (item 7): Boolean-semiring bit networks with arbitrary tables evade C1 and are exactly existential CSP projections (NP objects, unconditionally). Prop E2: under P=NP the graph of every NP set has a poly unambiguous network, whose B-, N- and Q-contractions coincide (existence -> counting). First failing step: the external theorems refute VP circuits, not small networks; small Q-networks exist unconditionally for VNP-hard tensors (Cook-Levin tableau for f_n); counterexample PERM support (T51 T-B).
Sec.4 (item 8): forced by P=NP: F1 deterministic uniquification (lex-first witness; Valiant-Vazirani unconditional only randomized), F2 NP in SPP, F3 G_E in VNP_p for every NP set E (unconditionally <=> NP in Mod_pP/poly by Valiant's criterion, from memory). All relativize (AW world 17590); not-F3 would be a G_E outside VNP, which no theorem supplies. No contradiction. First failing implication: P=NP forces nothing algebraic beyond VNP-type or relativizing statements. P!=NP has not been proved.

structure.conclusion: Formal functional QE VNP-complete (owner construction verified); existential vs formal vs semantic QE separated (E1); P=NP bridge existence->counting (E2) does not reach VP-level; forced properties F1-F3 relativizing; no contradiction

Setting: H_{G,q}(X) = OR_alpha AND_v X_{v,alpha|E(v)} on the r x r grid, d = r^2 groups; P = arithmetisation (GF(2) or Z) of a Boolean circuit of size S for H, deg P <= d+k. structure.conclusion: UCC STRENGTH CHECK (owner proposal 'UNIFORM COMPUTATION COMPRESSION' 2026-11-26, director check; CLAIMED). (0) Owner's quantitative target confirmed: under P = NP, MMW/CHMY give T(N, N^mu) <= N^{1+c mu} for a fixed unknown c, so a bound T(N, N^mu) >= N^{1+delta} with fixed delta for all small mu is sufficient (consistent with seq 17325/17328: no bound of the form N s^{c'} with fixed c' suffices). (1) UCC => P != NP: verified (P = NP => Q in DTIME(m^c) => every L_k in DTIME(n^{a max(1,c)}), contradicting the time hierarchy for k > a max(1,c)). (2) EQUIVALENT FORM: UCC <=> there are j, b with P contained in Sigma_j TIME(n^b) (=>: Q in Sigma_j TIME(m^d) composed with R_k; <=: Sigma_j-SAT is complete for Sigma_j TIME(n^b) under n^b polylog-time reductions). So UCC asserts a polynomial speedup of ARBITRARY degree of deterministic time by bounded alternation; it implies P != PH. No such speedup is known (known for multitape TMs: constant-factor / log-factor alternation speedups such as Paul-Pippenger-Szemeredi-Trotter). (3) RANDOM-ORACLE SEPARATION: for a random oracle A, P^A != NP^A with probability 1 (Bennett-Gill), but UCC^A fails with probability 1: L^A = parity of A on the first n^k strings is in DTIME^A(n^{k+1}); a Sigma_j TIME^A(n^b) machine is a depth-(j+1) circuit of size 2^{O(n^b)} with bottom fan-in n^b over these n^k oracle bits, which by Hastad's correlation bound agrees with parity on a negligible fraction once k > b j (+O(1)); countably many machines. Hence UCC is strictly stronger than P != NP in the relativised sense, and any proof must be non-relativising and must fail in a world where P != NP holds. CLASSIFICATION under the owner rule of 2026-11-26: a new conditional chain whose antecedent implies P != NP; it does not shrink an existing gap; not adopted as a FruitStack target unless the owner overrides. Not a gap closure.

structure.conclusion: KERNEL-CUT-RANK (owner derivation 2026-11-26, director check; CLAIMED). K_G over F_q (q = 3): x_v in F_q^3 with sum 0, z_{e,i} = -x_{u,i} - x_{v,i}, dim K_G = 2|V|; T_G = indicator of K_G. VERIFIED BY AUTHOR: (i) for every linear K and coordinate split L|R the flattening of 1_K is a disjoint union of all-ones blocks indexed by K/(K_L + K_R), so its rank is q^{dim K - dim K_L - dim K_R} over every coefficient field (this is the matroid connectivity lambda_K(L) and the minimal-trellis state-space dimension of a linear code at a cut, classical: Forney, Muder); (ii) for a vertex split U|U' and any placement of the edge coordinates, every crossing edge forces one endpoint to lose both degrees of freedom, also when the three z_{e,i} are split between the sides (then one endpoint receives >= 2 coordinates); the endpoints losing 2 form a vertex cover, the optimum is a minimum cover, and Koenig gives min rank = q^{2 nu(G[U,U'])} (= 9^nu); (iii) bounded-degree expanders give 2^{Omega(|V|)} for every balanced vertex split. STRENGTH: membership in K_G is a linear system (3|E| mod-3 checks, O(|E|) gates; one-pass in a good order with about lambda log q bits), so the cut rank is exactly tight for cut-respecting models (deterministic communication across that cut, fixed-order ROBP/OBDD width, fixed-order streaming space) and gives nothing for general circuits; consistent with the open question of seq 8834 ('a large invariant alone cannot imply hardness'). For varying-cut sums (Raz-type random-partition arguments) the rank q^{2 nu} is a constant fraction of the exponent below the maximal flattening rank of a balanced coordinate split, while such arguments need near-maximal rank; and 1_K = prod_j (1 - l_j^2) is a product of 3|E| quadratics. Consequence: any hardness must come from the Boolean Exact-One restriction (K_G intersected with the Exact-One set), not from the kernel; that intersection is the object the next step must treat. Width theorem w* = 2 tw(G)+1 itself: Lean-checked (seq 4058, 4079), novelty question open (seq 8795). Not a gap closure.

WEIGHTED-SUBST (owner bound 2026-11-26, director check and split; CLAIMED; within CONV-D seq 17216). F(x) = V(A(x)), A = anti-checker generator outputting t labelled positions (y_i, x_{y_i}), V = consistency predicate on T = t(m+1) bits. Substituting a formula for each output bit A_j at each of its mu_j(V) occurrences gives exactly L(F) <= sum_j mu_j(V) L(A_j); sum_j mu_j(V) = L(V). Director split, with t = N^{K beta}: (R1) L(V) <= N^{2+beta-Delta} is needed; V is an NP predicate on T = N^{O(beta)} bits, so ANY fixed polynomial bound L(V) <= T^C (C independent of beta) suffices for small beta - but NP subset P/poly gives V only circuits; R1 is 'V in Formula[poly]', supplied by NP subset Formula[poly] (OPS's stronger hypothesis), not by NP subset P/poly. Lower bound for R1: fixing the position inputs restricts V to H_{J,a}, so by PARTIAL-MCSP-LB seq 17211 (u = K beta) L(V) >= t^{2+1/K-o(1)}, and V has >= t^{2+1/K-o(1)} value-bit leaves - polynomial, consistent with R1. (R2) Given R1, max_j L(A_j) <= N^{2+beta-Delta-CK beta} suffices: every anti-checker output bit needs a SUBQUADRATIC formula; the weights mu_j matter only up to the factor L(V) = N^{O(beta)}.
