statement: SHAPLEY GAMES ON CLAUSE GADGETS OF G_phi (owner idea 2026-11-27; PI; CLAIMED, Claude family). Players are the clause gadgets. By parsimony (17584) #Col^pin(G_S) = #SAT(phi_S). G1: v(S) = 1[phi_S UNSAT], a simple monotone game whose minimal winning coalitions are the MUSes, so Sh is the Shapley-Shubik index. Lemma G1: a clause in no MUS is a null player, Sh = 0. Proof: if v(S+c) - v(S) = 1 then S+c contains an MUS, and that MUS contains c. G2: v(S) = n - log2 #SAT(phi_S). Efficiency: sum of Sh = n - log2 #SAT(phi), an exact decomposition of solution-space information over the gadgets. Marginal of c at S = -log2 Pr[c | phi_S]. Lemma G2 (Harris): if every variable occurs with only one polarity, all clause events are increasing after flipping, so Pr[c | phi_S] >= 7/8 and Sh_c <= log2(8/7). Checks (scratch shapley/shap.py): G1 25 UNSAT instances (n=5, m=16): efficiency exact, non-MUS clauses 64/64 with Sh = 0. G2 25 instances (n=10, m=12): efficiency error < 1e-15. Harris bound: 480 clauses, 0 violations (max 0.1668 vs 0.1926). Not a step that fails in the AW world (17590): exact Shapley values are #P-type, FPSPACE.

DECOUPLE-ACCOUNTING (director, 2026-11-26; CLAIMED). The only upper-bound mechanism under NP subset SIZE[n^a] is QO1 (seq 16795): circuits of size (input length) * s^K, K = K(a). Old regime: circuit N^{1+K beta}, formula target below N^{2+beta}: required conversion exponent e_old = log(formula)/log(circuit) = 2 - (2K-1)beta/(1+K beta). Decoupled regime: circuit for H is t a^K = N^{1+beta-gamma+K beta}, target below N^{2+3beta-2gamma}: e_new = 2 - (2K-1)beta/(1-gamma+(1+K)beta). For K > 1/2 and every gamma > beta, e_new < e_old: the conversion must be STRICTLY more efficient; the optimum of the family is gamma -> beta (the old regime). e_new <= 1 once gamma >= 1-(K-2)beta: then the formula would have to be smaller than the QO1 circuit, which no conversion gives - the 't^{3-delta}' target near gamma = 1 needs a better upper bound than QO1, not a conversion. The approach to exponent 3 in t is an artefact of the shorter input (theta = beta/u -> 1 raises both the CJW exponent 2+theta and the QO1 exponent 1+K theta). FAIL-FAST: for DETERMINISTIC streaming algorithms with space S=(log n)^f, simple counterexamples always EXIST: take the explicit set X of 2^S+1 strings with polylog descriptions; by pigeonhole two x != x' share the state after the first half, and for the fooling set {(x, not x)} one of (x, not x'), (x', not x) is answered wrongly; complements of simple strings are simple. So the obligation is NOT existence but UNIFORM SELECTION: one polylogtime-uniform AC0 family must print a bad input at infinitely many lengths without advice, i.e. predict the collision index of A uniformly in n; for randomized A, collisions in distribution. Route G is the same obstacle (failures among simple inputs).

T-NORM-E (elementary variant, CONDITIONAL on D4): if C|rho computes PARITY_k as OR_a F_a with pairwise disjoint 1-sets (D4), every nonzero F_a implies PARITY_k and therefore reads all k live variables (flipping an unread variable keeps F_a = 1 and flips parity); so all F_a of leaf size < k give C|rho = 0, contradiction. The kernel incidence of the cubic preprint is the conormal correspondence of det_n. (a) LEMMA: every distribution whose samples all have CC <= s and which eps'-fools all n-input ROBPs of width >= 2 satisfies s log s >= Omega(log(1/eps')). statement: HYBRID ELIMINATION (owner theorem 2026-11-27, dual affine compression; PI proof check and implementation; CLAIMED, Claude family). (1) Statement checked. Over F3, {l=1} cup {l=2} = complement of {l=0}. Represent S = {Ex = e} minus union B_i. If x_j is determined by the linear part (x_j = f(y)), then pi(S) = {E'y = e'} minus union T^{-1}(B_i) with T(y) = (y, f(y)). The preimage of an affine set under an affine map is affine or empty, so k_after <= k_before. Proof correct: y is in pi(S) iff T(y) is in S, because x_j is unique. (2) Implementation (scratchpad/aelim/hybrid.py). B_i are kept reduced modulo E, so parallelism is detected modulo E. Two forbidden hyperplanes l=c1, l=c2 become the equation l=c3; three mean UNSAT. A variable that occurs in E is eliminated by substitution, otherwise by merge.eliminate_m. Validation: 0/300 mismatches against brute force on random hybrid instances (r <= 6). (3) Controls (scratchpad/aelim/hyb_ctrl.log). Gauss control, same instances as 17918: peak forbidden count 0 at every stage for k = 6, 7, 8, 12, 20, against 34-48 before. The procedure now stays inside Gaussian elimination, as predicted. 1-in-3 with clauses as equations and z != 2 as forbidden hyperplanes, m = 0.62N: peak 1-24 for N = 8..24, brute-force checked for N <= 9. 3-colouring: no linear part arises (each edge forbids one hyperplane, never a parallel pair), so hybrid = previous method. G peaks 1-3; Prism(G) gadgets-first peaks 66 (K3), 65 (P3), 98 (C5). The prism encoding costs much more in this representation; Fable Lemma J needs an extra brute-force re-simplification per gadget that is not implemented. (4) Meaning: the rule separates linear structure from the nonlinear part exactly. For 3-colouring the whole instance is nonlinear in this sense. Small sizes only; no asymptotic statement; counts measure the representation, not hardness (17917). No obligation closed.

statement:
T48 addendum sec.8 (owner's derivation, PI check). CLAIMED; cross-family review pending.
(Owner correction) Prop5.2 was checked against the literature. Second proof: IKW (NEXP in P/poly => NEXP=MA) and P=NP => MA in Sigma2 = P, which contradicts the hierarchy. Q-BD is excluded as a direct route to a contradiction with P=NP.
Thm8.1 (owner, checked): for a circuit D with s gates over F2, D^2-D = sum_i Q_i (x_i^2-x_i) formally, with all Q_i computed by one circuit of size O(s). Proof: e(a)=a^2-a; XOR: e(a)+e(b) (char 2); NOT: e(a); AND: b^2 e(a) + a e(b); backward weight propagation, O(1) per edge. Existence is trivial (I is the vanishing ideal); the content is the size O(s). The table holds only in char 2 and differs in char 3.
Cor8.2: C_n = E AND NOT E = E^2-E gets an O(s) certificate, checked by one formal identity test (coRP). The A2 counterexample of Thm4 is no barrier for A2 + formal identity + defect certificates; the Thm4 barrier still holds for A2.
Classification (search; full texts not read yet): certificates sum g_j f_j + sum h_i(x_i^2-x_i) measured by circuit size are the Grochow-Pitassi Ideal Proof System (FOCS 2014/JACM). It p-simulates Extended Frege; superpolynomial IPS lower bounds for tautologies imply VP != VNP. Thm8.1 is a linear-size IPS certificate for the Boolean defect; novelty is not claimed.
Prop8.3: Cor8.2 uses only the syntactic form E(1+E). For C' = E AND E~ (E~ a structurally different circuit for NOT E), a compact certificate of E+E~+1 in I (circuit equivalence) is needed. A uniform barrier for pieces+IPS would be an IPS lower bound, which implies VP != VNP; so for the extended class neither a saving proof nor an attainable barrier exists without algebraic circuit lower bounds. This is a classification, not a premise.
Q-BD consequence: separate the full normal form (ParityP-hard) from a compact certificate (Thm8.1). A saving needs polynomial-size certificates for the zero pieces on <= 2^n/n^{omega(1)} pieces, and an efficient way to find them (a search problem); this is open.

structure.conclusion: On rows = maxterms (maximal SAT) and columns = minterms (minimal UNSAT) of any monotone function, u strictly contained in v implies |v minus u| = 1 (u + c is UNSAT for c in v minus u and would be a proper subset of the minimal UNSAT v otherwise). Hence containment-incidence matrices (A[u,v] != 0 only for u contained in v, any signs) are single-difference families, capped at Gal ratio <= N by D-014f. Multi-difference support needs entries with u not contained in v.

INTEGER-LATTICE PARITY ALGORITHM for positive 1-in-3 SAT (owner 2026-11-27; owner proof, PI check; CLAIMED, Claude family only). Every Boolean solution satisfies Mx = 1 over Z. Smith/Hermite form (Kannan-Bachem, polynomial): no integer solution => unsatisfiable; else x = x0 + Kz, K a Z-basis of ker_Z M (d_Q = n - rank_Q M <= d_F3). e = rank_F2(K_H mod 2), H = variables with >= 3 occurrences: Boolean x_H is determined by its parity, so at most 2^e candidates; for each, check disjointness of covered clauses and decide the <= 2-occurrence residual by matching (deterministic). Time O*(2^e), e <= min(|H|, d_Q, d_F3); with the subspace sieve (17465) O*(2^{min(e,s)}) (two branches: deterministic e, randomized s). Example h+a+b = h+b+c = h+c+a = 1: |H| = d_Q = d_F3 = 1, e = 0. Check zlattice_check.py: 400 random instances (occurrences <= 4): 35 without integer solution, all unsatisfiable; 365 others: every Boolean solution's x_H in the 2^e candidates, algorithm = brute force 365/365; e < |H| in 235/365, e = 0 in 2/365. Integer solvability cross-checked against sympy Smith normal form 12/12. Random RX3C (each variable exactly 3 times): no integer solution in 54/60 (n=30) and 59/60 (n=60), i.e. a polynomial unsatisfiability certificate there; when solvable, e = 1. Strength: exact parameterized algorithm, elementary; novelty unchecked; hard structured instances (e.g. T41 Sec. 6/10b reductions) not measured. No lower bound, no P vs NP statement.

CONV-D (owner weakening 2026-11-26, director check; the obligation of TRUNC2 seq 17202 in exponent form). F_beta = Gap-MCSP[N^beta/(c log N), N^beta]; under NP subset SIZE[n^a], QO1 gives circuits S(F_beta) <= O(N^{1+K beta}), K = K(a). CJW20-GAP (seq 17198; any polylog gap factor, the proof's knobs are independent) gives L(F_beta) >= N^{2+beta-xi} for every xi > 0. A problem-dependent conversion L(F_beta) <= O(S(F_beta)^{2-d(beta)}) contradicts it iff d(beta)(1+K beta) > (2K-1)beta + xi; choosing xi = beta this holds whenever d(beta) > 2K beta/(1+K beta). Since K = K(a) is not known in advance, the uniform sufficient condition is limsup_{beta->0} d(beta)/beta = infinity (e.g. d = sqrt(beta)); no constant distance from exponent 2 is needed. This is R-DELTA (seq 17161) in exponent form. Open: any mechanism for such d(beta). Logical strength: the conversion under NP subset P/poly implies NP not in P/poly.

ST2 INDEPENDENT TRANSFER, STRENGTHENED (author Claude family; owner's sec. 9 argument with P = NP replaced by NP subset P/poly): let S be polylog-uniform AC0_d[2^{m^k}] with r CX rounds, uniformity time m^u. Bit i of X_j is a Sigma_{d'}-TIME[poly(m, L_j, log b)] predicate g_j(i, b, D_<j) with random access to the earlier answers D_<j (padding zeros beyond the description). Assume NP subset P/poly, so PH subset P/poly and Sigma_{d'} has circuits of size n^{c}. Induction: if every earlier answer has size <= m^{K_i}, hardwiring b and D_<j gives a circuit for X_j of size m^{K_j}, K_j = c*O(K_{j-1} + k + u), independent of b. For b > K* = max_j K_j the answer 'a circuit of size m^{K_j} for X_j' is admissible in every round (Teacher only has to exist, no uniformity needed), so X_r has circuit complexity <= m^{K*} < m^b at every large N: S fails for all b > K*. Hence: absolute protocol => NP notsubset P/poly (stronger than Thm 1.7's P != NP). Uses neither Lemma 5.4 nor SearchMCSP.

BIAS-FLOOR (director, 2026-11-26; check of the owner's global Fourier error balance for the Forbes-Kelley step; CLAIMED). Owner's identities verified: (i) Parseval + Cauchy-Schwarz: sum_S |f^(S)| <= sqrt(A) for f in {0,1} with A accepted inputs; (ii) for independent D_i, T_i, G_i: b_{D xor (T and G)}(S) = b_D(S) E_T b_G(S cap T), so |b_{G_{i+1}}(S)| <= delta_i and Delta <= delta_i sqrt(A); (iii) signed S0290 convolution f^(S) = 2^{-N} sum_{u_1+..+u_q >= T} prod_j D_{j,S}(u_j) for disjoint components (Walsh characters are multiplicative over the components). LEMMA (unconditional): for every F subset {0,1}^N with |F| = A and every distribution Y supported in F, max_{S nonempty} |b_Y(S)| >= (1 - A 2^{-N}) / sqrt(A). Proof: apply (i) to f = 1_F: 1 - A 2^{-N} = E f(Y) - E f(U) = sum_{S nonempty} f^(S) b_Y(S) <= max|b_Y| sqrt(A). CONSEQUENCE: with F = {CC <= s}, A <= 2^{O(s log s)}, the bias delta < 1/(6 sqrt A) required by the owner's balance cannot be achieved by ANY distribution whose outputs all have CC <= s; a generator that meets it necessarily has outputs of CC > s. The gap 'CC(G(z)) <= N^{mu+o(1)} versus the needed <= N^mu' is therefore not a lower-order technicality but a counting impossibility. Reason: the estimate uses only A and not the resources of M, so it would apply equally to f = 1_F itself. MECHANISM EXCLUDED (on confirmation): fooling the MCSP algorithm through a bias/Fourier-L1 bound that depends only on the number of accepted inputs, for every mu. Any working generator analysis must use the time/state bound of M (consistent with seq 17279 (c) and seq 17284).

QO4 REASSESSMENT OF EXISTING LOWER BOUNDS BY THE RATIO eps(beta)/beta: of 368 cross-family-survived lower-bound steps (lb_audit, 602 total) none is a superlinear lower bound for general (unrestricted fan-in-2) circuits; all concern restricted classes (formulas, low reuse, streaming/update maps, restricted residual circuits). Formulas: CJW20 gives N^{2+beta-eps} (ratio unbounded) but only for De Morgan formulas. D2 in the Q2 regime (size N^{1+k beta}): De Morgan circuits with r <= (1-(k-1)beta-eps')log2 N reused gates are excluded for every k once beta < (1-eps')/(k-1) (T07 + CJW20-T5.5-GAP). D5's quantifier objection (fixed eps against a budget vanishing with beta) disappears under Q2, because the target exponent k beta vanishes too; the magnitude gap stays: AF covers <= N^{beta-eta} reused gates, a size-N^{1+k beta} circuit may have up to N^{1+k beta}. RESULT: no existing result satisfies Q2/Q3/Q*; the weakening changes the residual's size bound, not its type.

COV1 COLLECTIVE COVERAGE (forall C exists i exists x R_i(C,x)), target size N^{1+k beta} (Q2): class K1 = B2/De Morgan circuits with r <= (1-(k-1)beta-eps')log2 N reused gates (B2 via D3: r+2t) -> excluded by T07+CJW20 (both owner-verified; T07 also Q-92b080505e:S0001 SURVIVED). K2 = circuits whose reused gates are narrow (d_g <= N^{1-beta-eta}) -> collapse under the CJW20 restriction (D6, derivation, unverified) and fall into K3. K3 = after restriction gamma <= N^{beta-eta} reused gates -> AF (conditional on P1 local PRG with error 2^{-gamma}, P2 forest shrinkage; unverified). RESIDUAL R = circuits of size N^{1+k beta} with more than N^{beta-eta} wide reused gates surviving the restriction: no mechanism. Streaming side: Q3/route M -> O*. The union K1-K3 is not yet a cover of all circuits; covering R is the obligation.

Transfer lemma: if S(F_n) is superpolynomial in N=C(n,3) for infinitely many n then NP not in P/poly, hence P != NP (sufficient, not necessary); the exact uniform equivalent is a superpolynomial lower bound for F_n against P-uniform circuits. Subfunction counting S >= log2 D_k - 1 is valid but capped at N-1 for every function; disjoint-copy amplification of fixed obstructions is capped at O(N).

Over GF(2) the clause system sum_{i in C} x_i = 1 is consistent for EVERY clause set (x_i = 1 for all i, since 3 = 1 mod 2); hence a GF(2) parity/consistency test never certifies unsatisfiability of positive 1-in-3-SAT. RC-ab0e62e4 (0 of 146 UNSAT detected) is this fact, not an empirical regularity; the 32% in D-016h is the CG-separated share of SAT instances.

statement: NONLINEAR OVERLAP EMBEDDING USCCL-NL (owner 2026-11-27; PI proof check; CLAIMED, Claude family). Phi: A^r -> K_G(A) surjective, A a finite abelian group, D_i = functional support of parameter i. Checked steps: (i) Phi restricted to the vertex blocks of X depends only on S_X, so |S_X| >= 2|X| (Hall condition); (ii) Delta = Phi(x') - Phi(x) lies in K_G(A) (subgroup), so a nonzero vertex block has >= 2 nonzero coordinates and two supports in the same 3-block meet; (iii) for an edge uv, i in S_u, j in S_v, either i in S_v or j in S_u (case ii), or both differences vanish on the far block and have >= 2 nonzero coordinates in the 3 edge coordinates, so they meet. Hence G[K2] embeds in H_Phi. Correct. Also correct, but trivial or negative: USCCL-GATE s_min = n+3m (output counting: at most 2n outputs can be free inputs, all 3n+3m coordinate functions are distinct); control theorem K_{n,n}: min tw(H) = 2n+1, yet a used-colour-set DP (8 states) computes Z_S in O(n) semiring operations, #Col3 = 6(2^n - 1). Consequence: the invariant constrains representations of the solution kernel, not decision algorithms. No lower bound.

structure.conclusion: ST0 SOURCE (eccc-TR25-045 rev.1, local paper.txt l.351-356, 1516-1530, 3005-3220): Thm 1.7: an absolute polylog-uniform AC0[qpoly] Student-Teacher protocol S(1^N, b) (b in binary) with oracle CX[phi_WSC, O(1)] solving SIZE[n^b]-Avoid (n = log N) for infinitely many b implies P != NP. Fixed-b protocols exist (Sec. 5, brute force). Proof = Lemma 5.5 (Chen et al. Lemma 2.5: under P = NP, output bits of polylogtime-uniform AC0 are Sigma_d-TIME[polylog] hence DTIME[polylog], circuit complexity polylog) + Lemma 5.6 (oracle removal). The WHUPs (Hyp. 5.9 etc.) are only used for the proof-theoretic consequences, not for Thm 1.7.

CJ2 SUFFIX WITHOUT SELECTION (owner derivation, checked): for u != v with sigma_A(u) = sigma_A(v) let y = u AND NOT v if that is nonzero (then DISJ(u,y)=0, DISJ(v,y)=1), else y = v AND NOT u (roles swapped); the case test is an OR of n bits (AC0). A answers both instances equally, so one of F1(n)=(u_n,y_n), F2(n)=(v_n,y_n) is wrong at each such n, and by pigeonhole one fixed family is wrong infinitely often; the theorem only needs existence of R_A. CC(y) <= CC(u)+CC(v)+O(1), so y stays simple. Remaining W-D obligation: uniform (polylogtime-uniform AC0) colliding prefix families u_n != v_n for every admissible deterministic A, infinitely often.

GRAPH FORMULA for the projection rank e of 17481 (owner 2026-11-27; owner proof, PI check; CLAIMED, Claude family only). Clause graph: clauses = nodes, 2-occurrence variables = edges, 1-occurrence variables = private. Cokernel of the column space per connected component: Z (bipartite, no private), Z/2 (non-bipartite, no private), 0 (private). Hence Bl = 1 - Ah integer-solvable <=> balance sum_L b_i = sum_R b_i per bipartite component and sum b_i = 0 mod 2 per non-bipartite component. With h = h0 + Lz (saturated kernel lattice of E, so L mod 2 has full column rank): e = |H| - rank_Q E - rank_F2(PL) if consistent, else unsatisfiable. Same parameter as 17481, computed without a Smith form of M. Check graph_e_check.py: formula = lattice e on 400/400 random instances. On the 3-colouring embedding F(G) (vertex clauses E(v_r,v_g,v_b), edge clauses E(u_c,v_c,w) with private w): edge-clause components have a private variable; vertex clauses of degree>=2 vertices are isolated nodes whose balance is the vertex clause itself; so e(F(G)) = 2|V_{deg>=2}| exactly (proof as stated; checked 40/40), i.e. 2^e = 4^|V| exceeds 3^|V| enumeration: the integer step absorbs exactly one degree of freedom per vertex. No lower bound, no P vs NP statement.

Tangent-space bound (Fall D tool): for any singular point X of perm_n, rank Hess(perm_n)(X) <= n^2 - dim_X Sigma, where Sigma=Sing(V(perm_n))={grad perm_n=0}. In particular the torus orbit (dim <= 2n-1) gives rank <= n^2-(2n-1), recovering the connected torus bound.
structure.justification: Hess(perm_n) is the Jacobian of the map grad(perm_n): C^{n^2}->C^{n^2}; Sigma = {grad perm_n = 0} is its zero locus, so the Zariski tangent space T_X Sigma = ker Hess, giving dim ker Hess >= dim_X Sigma, i.e. rank Hess <= n^2 - dim_X Sigma. Consequence: M_5=14 would follow if every connected singular point lies in a component of Sigma(perm_5) of dimension >= 11. Whether dim Sigma(perm_5) >= 11 on connected components is OPEN (singular-locus geometry of perm, 2024 literature).

structure.conclusion: D3 BASIS: B2 -> De Morgan for circuits: each XOR/XNOR gate becomes 3 De Morgan gates and both of its children acquire fan-out 2. A B2 circuit of size S with r reused gates and t parity gates becomes a De Morgan circuit of size <= 3S with <= r+2t reused gates. For FORMULAS the conversion is not polynomially size-preserving in the needed exponent (B2 shrinkage exponent is 1, parity), so CJW20-type bounds hold in the De Morgan basis; B2 results follow only through r+2t. CHOPRS20 almost-formulas are De Morgan, so frontier C is basis-consistent.
premises: T07: every De Morgan circuit C of size S with r gates of fan-out > 1 has formula size L(C) <= 2^r (2S+1)

structure.conclusion: FACTOR-WITNESS (director, 2026-11-26, answering the owner's T07-S0290 synthesis question; CLAIMED). Split the table into k aligned blocks x_1..x_k. Product factorisation (AND over blocks of [x_i has an a'-circuit]) or score folding (sum_i min_{C_i} D_i(C_i)) replaces the SHARED witness (exists C forall i) by independent witnesses (forall i exists C_i). Facts: CC(x_i) <= CC(x)+O(m) and CC(x) <= sum_i CC(x_i) + O(km). (i) VALID for Gap-MCSP[a,b], b = 10ma, when k <= c1 m: YES gives every block <= a+O(m) =: a'; NO gives some block > (b-O(km))/k > a'. (ii) INVALID for k >= c2 m: let block i be the table of an independent random circuit of size a/2; every block test accepts (CC <= a/2 < a', every D*_i = 0), while there are 2^{k Omega(a log a)} such tables and circuits of size S number 2^{O(S log S)}, so some such x has CC(x) >= Omega(k a) > b. The window is Theta(log N) components, tight up to constants. (iii) In the valid window the factorised formula is a sum of k Gap-MCSP formulas on N/k bits with constant gap, covered by CJW20-GAP (the proof's knobs are independent of the gap factor): exponent unchanged (BLOCK-EMB seq 17180, ratio invariance). MECHANISM EXCLUDED (on confirmation): component factorisation / score folding with independent per-component witnesses as an exponent-gaining conversion, for any number of components. Consequence for T07 (seq 16758, A1 semantic T07 seq 16774) + S0290: the enumeration over cut assignments can be factorised only where the coupling through the shared witness is removed, which is (i)-(ii); a remaining route needs a compression of the shared-witness coupling that is not a product over components. Not located in the current registry: the CAPP steps S0258/S0290 (other question state); their full proofs were not re-read here.

structure.conclusion: ST3 SANDWICH - EXACT STRENGTH OF THE TARGET (author Claude family): converse with r = 0: if some fixed L in PH (Sigma_d, time m^u) has a.e. superpolynomial circuit complexity (for every b, CC(L_m) > m^b for all large m), then S(1^N, b) = tt(L_m) is a 0-round absolute protocol (depth d+O(1), size 2^{poly(m)}, uniformity poly(m), b ignored). So: [exists L in PH, a.e. superpolynomial] => [absolute 0-round protocol] => [absolute r-round protocol] => NP notsubset P/poly => P != NP. The Teacher rounds move the target at most between the a.e. and the i.o. form of 'PH notsubset P/poly'. RIGOROUS EXCLUSION: 'counterexamples as the source of hardness' gives no leverage beyond a PH circuit lower bound; every round transformation is, under PH subset P/poly, a bounded-complexity composition, so fail-fast control B is exhaustive, not heuristic. The owner's controls A and B are instances of ST2.

SUBSPACE SIEVE for positive 1-in-3 SAT (owner 2026-11-27; owner proof, PI re-derivation and check; CLAIMED, Claude family only). Setup: weighted T41 matrix B(X) over char 2, joint Schur (17432): K = [[A,D],[D^T,0]] on T u R, |R| = nu. (1) rank D < nu => unsatisfiable. (2) Q = basis of the left kernel of D (|T| x r, r = |T|-nu), C = Q^T A Q, q_i = rows of Q. K_U invertible <=> [[C,Q_U^T],[Q_U,0]] invertible (both <=> rank Q_U = |U| and C nondegenerate on ker Q_U). Consequences: h with dependent rows q_i (i in E_h) is never true; h,g whose row spans do not form a direct sum are never true together (this also encodes E_h disjointness). (3) Char 2: det[[C,L^T],[L,0]] = sum_{|I|=k} det(L[:,I])^2 det C[complement of I]; hence with W = span of admissible rows, s = dim W, a basis change putting W on y_1..y_s: F satisfiable <=> Z(lambda) = [y_1...y_s] sqrt(det(J_s + Y'CY')) prod_h (1 + lambda_h prod_{i in E_h} l_i(y)) is nonzero. (4) Algorithm: random weights and lambda in a polynomial-size field of char 2, coefficient by sum over 2^s subsets plus interpolation in t; time O*(2^s), polynomial space, one-sided error <= (m+|H|)/|F| (only one satisfying selection must survive). Portfolio O*(2^{min(|H|, s, d)}), d = F_3 nullity of the clause matrix (algorithm R). Check: sieve_check.py, 90 random instances (occurrences <= 4): algorithm = brute force 90/90, no false positive or negative, direct formula 90/90; s < |H| in 2/90. Placement: instance of determinantal sieving (Eiben-Koana-Wahlstroem arXiv 2502.13654 Thm 5, O*(2^r), char 2) adapted to symmetric matrices with diagonal; novelty of the parameter s unchecked. Extreme case every variable exactly 3 times: B=0, nu=0, C=0, s=m=n (RX3C, NP-complete): no saving. Random RX3C: F_3 nullity 1-3 in 600/600 (n=30,60,120). No lower bound, no P vs NP statement.

SEP-MERGE-LB (owner derivation 2026-11-26, director checked; CLAIMED). Gap-MCSP[a,b], b = N^beta, a = b/(10m). Split the table into q equal dyadic blocks. Any realisation F = OR_{sigma in {0,1}^w} AND_{j<=q} F_{j,sigma}(x_j) (arbitrary local F_{j,sigma}) needs w >= B/2 = Omega_beta(N^beta) for q = C_beta m. Proof checked: B = Theta(a log a) a power of 2 with every B-bit table of circuit size <= a (Lupanov); the periodic tables y^{N/B} are 2^B YES instances (the circuit reads only the low log B index bits); blocks are dyadic of size >= B, so each block contains whole periods and distinct y give distinct block restrictions; a sigma accepting k patterns accepts their k^q block-wise mixtures (product of the A_{j,sigma}), none of which may be a NO instance, and at most 2^{O(b log b)} tables have CC <= b, so k <= 2^{O(b log b / q)} <= 2^{B/2} for q = C_beta m; hence 2^w >= 2^{B/2}. Tight up to a log factor: sigma = a size-b circuit description (O(b log b) bits) with F_{j,sigma}(x_j) = [x_j = block j of tt(sigma)] is a valid realisation, so w = Theta~_beta(N^beta). Type: nondeterministic q-party number-in-hand cover / fooling-set bound; novelty not checked. SCOPE: (1) block-faithful: after fixing sigma no condition reads two blocks; the recursive elimination of SEP-ELIM-LB flattens by distributivity to this form with w <= (#leaves) W_path, so with leaves = blocks W_path >= Omega_beta(N^beta / log N). (2) NOT a formula lower bound: formula size corresponds to Karchmer-Wigderson games (seq 3616), not to rectangle covers; the owner's equality example (cover 2^B, formula O(qB)) shows the gap. MECHANISM EXCLUDED (on confirmation): block-faithful separator / conditional-state enumeration, including a conditional S0290-style score convolution over shared variables in the OR_sigma AND_j form, as an exponent-gaining conversion for Gap-MCSP.

Any 'solution-count mod 3' Gal matrix A[u,v] = #solutions of the clause system u union v, taken mod 3, is identically zero: Boolean count = 0 because v is UNSAT; GF(3) count is 0 (inconsistent) or 3^d with d >= 1 (the all-ones direction j is always in the kernel), hence 0 mod 3. Solution counts mod 3 carry no information for positive 1-in-3; any useful count needs the j-direction quotiented out (count lines, i.e. 3^(d-1)).

structure.conclusion: A2 FAIL-FAST CONTROL FOR A: YES contains every table supported on any set T of m = N^beta/(c log N) positions (circuit size <= m log N). Hence |B_K^+| >= max_T |b_K(V_T)| for the coordinate subcubes V_T. Semantic compression therefore requires the reused-gate tuple b_K to take few values on EVERY sparse subcube - a property of the chosen cut gates, not of YES-instance sparsity. Combined with route B (YES side = PRG outputs G(z) o rho): |B^+_G| <= 2^{seed} while PRG error >= 2^{-seed}, so A o B gains only if the reused gates carry <= seed - O(log N) bits about the seed (same information threshold as D5).

ACCEPTANCE-TRIE (owner derivation 2026-11-26, director check; CLAIMED). Setting of seq 17306/17314: for an accepting crossing signature alpha (crossing records include state, time and input-head position), R_alpha = prod_j R_{alpha,j}, a_{alpha,j} = |R_{alpha,j}|, sum_alpha prod_j a_{alpha,j} = A (accepted inputs, disjoint by determinism). VERIFIED BY AUTHOR: (i) the trie of R_{alpha,j} has <= a_{alpha,j}+1 nodes per level (reject sink included), so w_{alpha,j} <= min(2^{O(B+log t)}, a_{alpha,j}+1); (ii) the per-alpha ROBP reads the parts J_{alpha,1}, J_{alpha,2}, ... one after another (legitimate: Forbes-Kelley fools arbitrary-order ROBPs) and collapses to accept/reject at part boundaries, so its width is max_j w_{alpha,j}; (iii) splitting each R_{alpha,j} into ceil(a/2^h) pieces of size <= 2^h gives an exact disjoint OR of K'(h) = sum_alpha prod_j ceil(a_{alpha,j}/2^h) ROBPs of width <= 2^h+1, and K'(h) = sum_alpha |R_alpha| 2^{-Phi_h(alpha)} = A E_X[2^{-Phi_h}] (X uniform on accepted inputs), log(w'K') <= h + 1 + log A - P(h). NEW LOWER BOUND (director): ceil(a/2^h) >= 1, so K'(h) >= K_acc := number of accepting signatures with R_alpha nonempty >= 2^{H(alpha(X))} for EVERY distribution X on accepted inputs; hence log(w'K') >= max(h, log K_acc). Replacing prefixes by residual (Myhill-Nerode) classes lowers the width further but leaves K' >= K_acc unchanged. CONSEQUENCES: (1) the trie attacks only point 1 of seq 17306 (width), never point 2 (crossing count); with the floor of seq 17284(2) any success needs s log s >~ log K_acc. (2) With seq 17314 on the Lupanov family: K_acc >= 2^{(rb-L)/(r-1)}, so for multiplicity r > L/b the trie gives no gain over the floor regime. (3) Jensen: P(h) <= E Phi_h <= E sum_j min(h, log a_{alpha,j}) <= E log|R_alpha| = log A - H(alpha(X)). So log(w'K') = N^{o(1)} REQUIRES (a) H(alpha(X)) <= N^{o(1)} and (b) E sum_j min(h, log a_{alpha,j}) >= log A - N^{o(1)} with h = N^{o(1)}: a typical accepted input has >= N^{mu-o(1)} information-carrying parts, each with <= 2^{N^{o(1)}} local completions, while its whole crossing signature has N^{o(1)} bits of entropy, i.e. the accepted set is up to 2^{N^{o(1)}} pieces a union of products with tiny factors and M is almost oblivious on accepted inputs across N^{mu} block visits. (4) The trade-off moves from the block length B to the local acceptance sizes: one block gives K_acc = 1, a = A, log w' = log A, which is exactly seq 17284(2). (5) The folded Cor-17 machine (seq 17279 (c)) is a correct decider, so (a)+(b) fails for it; a proof of (a)+(b) must use q = O(1). PRIOR ART: EXT prefix trie (owner 2026-11-20, seq 5364, 5389), D_t <= |Im|+1 (seq 10124, 17263), global trie decomposition (seq 17284(2)), residual classes (seq 6652, 12810, 13706). New: the per-part application, the K'(h) identity and the bound K' >= K_acc. Not a gap closure.

structure.conclusion: A*-STRENGTH (director, 2026-11-26; CLAIMED). (i) The open step 'L_R in PH' implies P != NP at once (L_R in PH minus P gives PH != P); A* is only the device certifying L_R not in P. More generally any refuter R* of A* (infinitely often) whose bit function is in PH gives a PH language outside P: the route is at least as strong as P != NP, not a reduction of it. (ii) L_R is hard for DTIME(m^{sqrt(log m)/2}) under polynomial-time reductions: for M deciding L' in that time, encode w in the m-bit number n_w and take the fixed program Q='decode w from n, run M(w)' of constant rank j0; then w in L' iff <n_w,j0> not in L_R. Hence L_R in PH iff (up to the constant in the exponent) DTIME(m^{Theta(sqrt log m)}) is contained in PH - a superpolynomial-time inclusion strictly stronger than P != NP. Relative to a PSPACE-complete oracle A, PH^A = P^A while the relativized time hierarchy keeps DTIME^A(m^{sqrt log m}) outside P^A, so the open step is false relative to A: any proof must be non-relativizing. (iii) Corrections to the 2026-11-26 review note: 'P=NP gives only polynomial, not polylogarithmic time' is wrong, since poly(m) = polylog(n); the refuter need not simulate A* over the stream (A*-REFUTER).

A1 SEMANTIC T07 (valid; = D4 restricted to occurring assignments): for a cut K whose removal leaves a formula forest, C'(x)=OR_{b in B_K^+}[all principal formulas consistent with b] AND out_b computes the Gap-MCSP promise problem (YES: the true assignment is in B_K^+; NO: a consistent b is the true one, so C'(x)=C(x)=0), L(C') <= |B_K^+|(2S+1). Contrapositive with CJW20-T5.5-GAP: every cut K of every correct De Morgan circuit of size S has |B_K^+| >= N^{2+beta-eps}/(2S+1).

EXCLUSION E-LEVIN (mechanism, not the statement): (a) for Levin's universal search U and every fixed algorithm A that outputs SAT witnesses, t_U(F) <= 2^{|A|} (t_A(F) + v(|F|)) with v the witness check time; hence 'U runs in polynomial time on all satisfiable F' <=> P = NP, and a lower bound for U is up to a constant factor a lower bound for every algorithm - the quantifier over algorithms is not removed. (b) Relative to an oracle A with P^A = NP^A (BGS, seq 3), U^A runs in polynomial time; every argument that uses U only through simulation and diagonalization relativizes and cannot show U superpolynomial. Excluded: pure simulation/diagonalization against U. Not excluded: arguments that use the Cook-Levin encoding of U's run non-black-box (short encodings of long computations); the only mechanism known to work there is the algorithmic method of Williams (succinct SAT), whose proven reach is NEXP/NQP lower bounds against ACC-type classes, not P != NP.

MATROID-CUT-RANK for P_B, corrected replacement of seq 17397 (owner 2026-11-27, director check; CLAIMED, needs review by another model family). (T1) rank_{u|v} prod_i (a_i(u) + b_i(v) + c_i)^2 >= 2^m when {a_i}_M and {b_i}_M are both independent (diagonal evaluation; extension field over F_3) - unchanged from 17397, correct. (T2) 2^kappa <= rank <= (D+1)^kappa, kappa = matroid-intersection number at the cut - unchanged, correct. (T3') WEIGHTED GLOBAL SEPARATOR (owner): for any basis B, order pi, p = max over prefix cuts of kappa, and any S subset V (h = |S| >= 1): take a prefix cut with dim pi_S(L) = h and Edmonds' J (a + b <= p); L', R' as in 17397; V_L, V_R = vertices of G where L' resp. R' are nonzero. Support lemma (seq 4071 argument) gives V_L, V_R disjoint and non-adjacent; dim L' + dim R' >= 2|V| - a - b and dim L' <= 2|V_L| give |D| <= p/2 for D = V minus (V_L u V_R); |V_L n S| <= (h + b)/2, |V_R n S| <= (h + a)/2. Separation (V_L u D, V_R u D) is 1_S-balanced (each side <= 2h/3) when h >= 3p; for h < 3p use (V, X) with X subset S, |X| = ceil(h/3) <= p. So every {0,1}-weighting has a w-balanced separation of order <= p. Robertson-Seymour (Graph Minors II, as quoted in Dvorak-Norin arXiv:1408.3869 v2 Sec. 1; checked at that source, RS original not read): tw(G) < 4p. Checked line by line by the director: correct. Dvorak-Norin's 15p (owner's first version) is also valid but superseded by 4p. RESULT (CLAIMED): min over kernel bases B and orders pi of the formal roABP width of P_B >= 2^p > 2^{tw(G)/4}. STRENGTH unchanged from 17397: unconditional lower bound for roABP after invertible linear change of variables, one explicit product of squared affine forms with small depth-3 circuits; w* (seq 4079) not used in the proof (2^{(w*-1)/8} is substitution); not related to M9; novelty of T1/T2 unchecked; no consequence for P != NP.

ADAPT-LB (owner derivation 2026-11-26, director check; CLAIMED; strengthens NONADAPT-LB seq 17222). b = N^beta, a = b/(10m), beta fixed. (i) Small YES circuits: split the m index bits into q = O(1/beta) groups of beta m/2 bits, decode every group completely (O_beta(N^{beta/2}) = o(a) gates); each one-position is then an AND of q decoded lines, so ANY set of r = a/(2q) = Theta_beta(b/m) ones has an a-circuit (previously r = Theta(a/m)). (ii) A uniform table with exactly R = C_beta b ones is a NO instance with prob 1-o(1): C(N,R) = 2^{Omega(R log(N/R))} against 2^{O(b log(b+m))} circuits. (iii) A one-sided algorithm (YES always accepted) cannot reject while it has seen <= r ones, since the table with exactly the observed ones is a YES instance consistent with every answer. Each new adaptive query hits a one with prob <= R/(N-t), so E X_t <= tR/(N-t) and Pr[reject] <= Pr[X_t > r] <= O_beta(t m/N); averaging over the NO-heavy distribution gives a fixed NO instance, so t = Omega_beta(N/log N) for adaptive and non-adaptive one-sided algorithms. Director scope note: CJW20 and CONV-D allow TWO-SIDED error; for two-sided algorithms the same distributions (YES: uniform r-subset, NO: uniform R-subset) give only t = Omega(N/R) = Omega_beta(N^{1-beta}) (views are all-zero with prob >= 1 - tR/N under both). Query bounds of order N/polylog do not constrain CONV-D, whose formulas have size >= N anyway; they exclude only bit-selection (sampling) as the conversion mechanism.

statement: SUPPLEMENT TO 17921: PRISM RANK, BLOCK ENCODING AND EXACT OVERLAP GRAPH (owner derivations 2026-11-27; PI checks and implementation; CLAIMED, Claude family). (1) Rank correction (owner). The prism equations top-sum, bottom-sum, d0 = d1, d1 = d2 are dependent, because (d0-d1) - (d1-d2) = d0+d1+d2 over F3. Normal form: t0+t1+t2 = 0, d0 = d1, d1 = d2, t0 != t1, d0 != 0; 3*2*2 = 12 colourings. 17921 adds all triangle equations and lets rref take the rank. The measured rank deficit equals the number of prisms exactly: K3-H 23 equations, rank 17, 6 prisms; P3-H 22/16/6; C5-H 36/26/10. This confirms the correction; the linearization and solution sets are unaffected. (2) Block encoding (owner). Pinned R = (0,1,2), p = dA, q = dB in {1,2}: a = p, b = 1+q, x = -1-p-q. Exactly (p,q) = (2,1) is forbidden; (1,1) -> 0, (2,2) -> 1, (1,2) -> 2. Edges of G become p_u+q_u != p_w+q_w; all other gadget variables are eliminated by affine substitution. Implementation scratchpad/aelim/block.py; the decoded solution set equals Col3(G) bijectively on 150 random graphs (0 mismatches). Hybrid elimination on the block form (vars 2n; start = 3n + m forbidden subspaces): K3 12 -> peak 12, P3 11 -> 11, C5 20 -> 20 (SAT); K4 18 -> peak 22 (UNSAT, grows). G itself needs only m. The block form is exact and needs no per-node gadget elimination, but it is not smaller than G. Observation (PI): with p' = p-1, q' = q-1 in {0,1}, the forbidden pair is (1,0), so the constraint is p' <= q' and the colour is -(p'+q'). The prism gadget is a thermometer (order) encoding of a ternary variable; the name 'order encoding' is from SAT practice, cited from memory. (3) Overlap theorem (owner). The primal graph of the residual constraints p_v != 0, q_v != 0, p_v - q_v != delta, p_u+q_u != p_w+q_w is H_rest = G[K2] (lexicographic product) for pinned R, and K1 join G[K2] for free delta = R1 - R0. The remaining reference coordinate (global translation) is isolated. Proof: edge constraints give complete bipartite joins between adjacent blocks; the block constraint gives p_v q_v; delta occurs in every block constraint. Check: primal graphs computed from the implemented constraints equal G[K2] and K1 join G[K2] on 200 random graphs with n <= 7, including isolated vertices (scratchpad/aelim/overlap.py; 0 mismatches). Width consequence: a universal vertex raises treewidth and pathwidth by exactly 1, so tw/pw(free) = tw/pw(G[K2]) + 1. From memory, unverified: tw(G[K_t]) = t(tw(G)+1) - 1, giving 2 tw(G) + 1 for pinned R. (4) Meaning: the overlap pattern G K_2 of USCCL-NL (17585) reappears exactly in the reduced prism representation. Two independent routes, the kernel parametrization and the implemented elimination, give the same graph structure. This holds for the stated parametrization before graph-dependent simplifications such as linearizing G's own triangles. USCCL is used only as min_B mu(H_B) = mu(G K_2). Not a computational lower bound; no obligation closed.

structure.conclusion: TRUNC (owner construction, director check; CLAIMED). D^(tau)_I=min(tau,D_I) composes exactly: D^(tau)_{I u J}=min(tau, D^(tau)_I + D^(tau)_J). Node state: BOT if no a-circuit is tau-close on I, else (C_I, E_I) with |E_I|<tau, S=O(a log a + tau m)=O(N^beta) bits; BOT at any node implies D* >= tau (reject). Director: (C_I,E_I) is LOSSLESS for x_I and is itself a circuit of size <= a + c m tau <= b (correction by minterms), so the scheme is exactly an MMW tree whose gates are GAP-Merge gates (find any tau-close a-circuit, must succeed when an exact one exists); FOURIER-SUP does not apply because far tables all map to BOT. DILEMMA (director): tau=1 gives exact gates, so MERGE-EXACT-LB applies and local conversion fails; tau>1 gives gates outside CJW20 but the root then decides only Gap-MCSP, and CJW20 Thm 5.5 (exact, fixed threshold) gives no contradiction. A contradiction then needs a Gap-MCSP formula lower bound N^{2-delta+K beta}; the book's best Gap bound is far below that (MECH-RANGE seq 17158), so this horn is the QO2/Q2 obligation (eps/beta -> infinity). CORRECTION of the review note's item 6: comparing N^{2-delta+K beta} with N^{2+beta-xi} is valid only for EXACT MCSP. Open check: whether CHOPRS Lemma 22 (ECC transfer exact -> approximate MCSP) keeps both the YES side (CC(Enc x) <= poly CC(x)) and formula cost; the paper is not in the local literature.

MMW-UNFOLD (cost of the K1/MMW route, Q-5d167697b4; MMW19 Lemma 3.1 as verified in seq 10407: size O~(N s/l), depth O(log N / log l), Circuit-Min-Merge[s] gates with l-bit input, l >= s^2; tree with fan-out 1, seq 9992): replacing every gate by a De Morgan formula of size l^b and unfolding, each input bit of a gate is read up to l^{b-1} times on average, so the child subformula is copied that often per level; over depth log N/log l the total formula size is about N^{b+O(beta)}. A contradiction with CJW20 (N^{2+beta-xi}) therefore needs b < 2 - Theta(beta): the GATE function Circuit-Min-Merge[s] on l = N^{2beta} bits must have SUBQUADRATIC formulas. NP subset P/poly gives the gates circuits of size l^a and no formula bound at all (even NP subset Formula[poly] gives only some fixed b, not b < 2). Hence the middle formula L(C_MMW) <= N^{2-delta} s^K is the R-MCSP-type obligation for an MCSP-like function at scale l (self-similar), not a weaker obligation. Open as before; it does not bypass R-MCSP.

CONSTANT-TEMPERATURE CORRELATION AMPLIFIER (owner 2026-11-27; PI check of every bound; exact M^3 by fractions; CLAIMED, Claude family). Input: G_phi from the switch-vertex construction (17497/17506), always 3-colourable, n vertices, with a pair (u,v) such that phi in SAT iff some proper colouring has sigma(u) = sigma(v) (the pair (t,T) of 17497 (3)). STEP A: add r = 2n+3 new vertices, each adjacent to u and v. Then Z(0) = 2^r A + B (A, B = colourings with equal or different colours at u, v; A+B <= 3^n). UNSAT: A = 0, so p_r = 0. SAT: p_r >= 2^r/(2^r+3^n) >= 8/9, since 2^{2n+3} >= 8*3^n. STEP B: T = 1/ln 2, so the conflict weight is 1/2 and M = J - I/2. M^3 = (1/8)[[41,42,42],...] (eigenvalues 125/8 and -1/8); M^2 has ratio 9/8 > 1, so an odd length is required. Replace each of the |E| edges of the N-vertex amplified graph by k = 42(2N+4) internally disjoint paths of length 3. The marginal on the original vertices is then proportional to q^{H(tau)} with q = (41/42)^k <= e^{-(2N+4)}. Proper colourings exist, so the conflict mass is <= 3^N q < 0.0075 < 1/16. RESULT: UNSAT gives P(sigma(u)=sigma(v)) <= 1/16; SAT gives >= (15/16)(8/9) = 5/6. The graph has size O(|E| N k) = poly(n). Hence approximating this two-point correlation at fixed T within additive error < 37/96 is NP-hard under polynomial-time many-one reductions. STRENGTH: relative hardness only, with unbounded degree. Known-type: inapproximability of the antiferromagnetic Potts model beyond uniqueness, already for bounded degree (Galanis-Stefankovic-Vigoda; from memory, verify), is stronger. No unconditional lower bound and no obligation closed.

K0 (unconditional depth class for COV1): a De Morgan circuit of depth D unfolds to a formula with <= 2^D leaves; a B2 gate is a De Morgan formula using each input at most twice, so B2 depth D gives <= 4^D leaves. With CJW20-T5.5-GAP: Gap-MCSP[N^beta/(Km), N^beta] has no De Morgan circuit of depth < (2+beta-eps)log2 N and no B2 circuit of depth < (1+beta/2-eps/2)log2 N, of any size. This is the full reach of the verified results under the MMW19 joint size-depth condition: Thm 1.4 b.3 needs depth poly(s) >= polylog N; b.2 (NC1 conclusion only) needs every c log N.

D4 REUSE-TO-CORRELATION DECOMPOSITION (exact): let C be a De Morgan circuit with gamma gates g_1..g_gamma of fan-out > 1 and S gates. For a in {0,1}^gamma let F_a(x) = AND_j [P_j(x,a) = a_j] AND P_out(x,a), where P_j, P_out are the principal formulas (CHOPRS20 Thm 30) with reused gates replaced by constants a. Then L(F_a) <= S+gamma, the F_a have pairwise disjoint supports and C = OR_a F_a. For any two distributions Y, Z: Pr_Y[C]-Pr_Z[C] = sum_a (Pr_Y[F_a]-Pr_Z[F_a]), so some formula F_a of size <= S+gamma has advantage >= Adv(C)/2^gamma. Reuse costs a factor 2^gamma in CORRELATION, not in size (T07 pays it in size).

MECH-RANGE (parameter check against OPS21/Q2, seq 16795-16796): in AF with a PRG of seed s^{c+o(1)} (CKLM19: c = 1/3, seq 16757), stars >= N^{beta+eta/2} force p >= N^{beta+eta/2-1}; with the unconditional worst case s = p L, L = N^{1+eps} (D4-SIM), seed <= N^{beta-eta} needs c(beta + eta/2 + eps) <= beta - eta, so eps/beta < 1/c - 1 (c = 1/3: eps < 2beta). Hence eps(beta)/beta stays bounded for every fixed c and the mechanism cannot reach Q2 without a structural change. Two levers only: (i) c -> 0, a PRG for size-s De Morgan formulas with seed s^{o(1)}, which implies a function in E without polynomial-size De Morgan formulas (open, far beyond the known n^{3-o(1)}); (ii) a bound on the number m of principal formulas: with a Tal-type forest bound (P2) s <~ p^2 L + p sqrt(m L), Q2 requires m <= N^{1-eps+4beta-7eta} at total size N^{1+eps} with eps/beta -> infinity. The 'fundamental change' asked for by the owner is therefore a reduction of m (count of reused gates), not of W; this is a necessary condition, not a construction.

MATROID-CUT-RANK for P_B (owner derivation 2026-11-27, director check; CLAIMED, needs review by another model family). (T1) Field F, P(u,v) = prod_i (a_i(u) + b_i(v) + c_i)^2, no factor the zero polynomial. If M (|M| = m) has {a_i}_M and {b_i}_M both linearly independent, then rank_{u|v}(P) >= 2^m (formal coefficient rank). Check: u_s with a_i(u_s) = t_i + s_i d_i, v_r with b_i(v_r) = -t_i - c_i - (1 - r_i) d_i; selected factor = (s_i + r_i - 1) d_i, so P(u_s, v_r) = 0 for s != r. Diagonal: every other factor is a nonzero polynomial in (t, d, free coordinates) (if a_j, b_j lie in the spans with coefficients lambda, mu, identical vanishing forces lambda = mu and lambda_i (2 s_i - 1) = 0, hence a_j = b_j = 0 and the factor is the nonzero constant c_j^2); the product of all diagonal factors and all d_i is a nonzero polynomial, so a good point exists over an infinite field. Over F_3 take an extension field: coefficient-matrix rank is invariant under field extension, and evaluation rank <= coefficient rank. Correct. Same mechanism as Lemma M9b' (seq 5192: diagonal evaluation + generic avoidance of the other factors); new is independence in place of variable-disjointness. (T2) Upper bound: with Edmonds' partition J (a = rk B_L[J], b = rk B_R[I \ J]), rank <= (D+1)^{a+b}; hence 2^kappa <= rank <= (D+1)^kappa, kappa = matroid-intersection number of the two row matroids at the cut. Correct. (T3) Application to K_G (q = 3, dim 2|V|), any basis B, any order pi, p = max over prefix cuts of kappa: for every vertex set S (h = |S|) a prefix cut with dim pi_S(L) = h exists; L' = {l in L : l|_J = 0}, R' = {r in R : r|_{I \ J} = 0}; S_L and S_R are disjoint (two nonzero vectors with coordinate sum 0 in F_3^3 share a support coordinate) and non-adjacent (if v in S_L, w in S_R then L'|_w = 0 and R'|_v = 0, so z_e = -x_v resp. -x_w have >= 2 of 3 nonzero edge coordinates on opposite sides of J: contradiction); |S_L| >= (h-a)/2, |S_R| >= (h-b)/2, separator D = S minus (S_L u S_R) with |D| <= p/2. Correct. CORRECTION (constant): components can still be (h+p)/2 > h/2, while Dvorak-Norin (from memory: every subgraph has a separator leaving components <= |V(H)|/2, of order k => tw <= 15k; verify at source) needs 1/2-balance. One more round on the large component (h >= 3p), else remove ceil(h/2) <= 1.5p vertices, gives order <= 1.5p, so tw(G) <= 22.5 p; the claim tw <= 15 p is not proved as written. RESULT (CLAIMED): min over kernel bases B and orders pi of the formal roABP width of P_B >= 2^{tw(G)/23} (Nisan: width = max prefix coefficient rank). STRENGTH: an unconditional lower bound for 'roABP after an invertible linear change of variables' on one explicit product of squared affine forms; P_B has small depth-3 circuits. w* = 2 tw + 1 (seq 4079) is NOT used in the proof; writing 2^{(w*-1)/46} is substitution only. The shared ingredient is the support lemma of the w* lower bound (seq 4071). Not related to M9 (IPS certificates of Psi_n). Literature novelty of T1/T2 (rank of products of linear forms vs matroid intersection) not checked. No consequence for P != NP.

THEOREM (non-equidimensionality): Sigma(perm_5)=Crit(perm_5) is NOT equidimensional over C; it has irreducible components of dimension 11 and 15. (First explicit proof of non-equidimensionality of the permanent critical locus for n=5; the 11-dim component is not in Xie arXiv:2609.27320, which gives only the global max dim 15 and disclaims equidimensionality.)
structure.justification: 11-dim component: F={diag(B',C'): perm_2(B')=0, perm_3(C')=0} is irreducible (perm_2,perm_3 irreducible hypersurfaces) of dim (4-1)+(9-1)=11, F subset Sigma. Witness X_A=diag([[1,1],[1,-1]], [[-2,-2,2],[-2,0,-1],[0,2,1]]): perm_2(B)=perm_3(C)=0, block gradients invertible (det -2, det 64), perm_5(X_A)=0, grad=0, rank Hess=14 (exact sympy), so dim T_{X_A}Sigma=11; hence 11=dim F <= dim_{X_A}Sigma <= dim T=11 => dim_{X_A}Sigma=11, smooth point of a unique 11-dim component. 15-dim component: L={rows 0,1 zero} is linear of dim 15, L subset Sigma (two zero rows kill all 4-minors). Witness X_B (rows 0,1 zero, rows 2-4 ones): grad=0, rank Hess=10 => dim T=15=dim L => smooth. Verified THREE ways: exact sympy (ranks 14/10, det G -2/64); independent reasoning model gpt-oss-120b (full argument VALID, 'fully rigorous'); CherryMe adversarial review (in progress).

structure.conclusion: AC-FAMILY-LB (owner derivation 2026-11-26, director check; CLAIMED; novelty vs. literature not confirmed - CHOPRS Cor 61 refutes the OPS Anti-Checker Hypothesis by a different route). b = N^beta, a = b/(10m), constants beta, zeta > 0. Let J_1..J_l be a FIXED (input-independent) family with |J_i| <= N^{1-zeta}. Uniform table with exactly R = D b ones (NO w.p. 1-o(1), as in ADAPT-LB seq 17227). By ADAPT-LB (i) any r = Theta_beta(b/m) ones have an a-circuit, so J_i is an anti-checker only if X_i = |J_i n ones| >= r. Hypergeometric tail: Pr[X_i >= r] <= (e|J_i|R/(N r))^r = (O_beta(m N^{-zeta}))^r = 2^{-Omega_{beta,zeta}(b)}. Union bound: for l <= 2^{c b} (c small) some NO instance has no anti-checker in the family. So a fixed family needs l >= 2^{Omega_{beta,zeta}(N^beta)} members. Any rule using only the family's consistency bits sees on that NO instance exactly what it sees on 0^N (a YES instance), so it accepts; an AND-of-tests formula over such a family has >= l leaves. MECHANISM EXCLUDED (on confirmation): fixed families of sublinear anti-checker candidates, any polynomial (even 2^{c N^beta}) size. NOT excluded: input-dependent anti-checkers; sets of size N^{1-o(1)}. CORRECTION of the scope note in seq 17222 ('does NOT constrain families'): fixed families are constrained by this count.

Slice route: level-m slices of f_n are coNP-hard (padding); monotone and general circuit size are polynomially related on slices (Berkowitz), so a superpolynomial monotone bound for them would prove P != NP (equivalent reformulation). Span-program analogue: mSP and SP polynomially related on slices, loss SP >= (mSP - 2N)/(N-1): all PNP-001 bounds (<= N+1) vanish under transfer. Generic Gal constructions on slices are natural-proofs-blocked (assuming NC^1 PRFs); a method must use function-specific structure.

statement: THEOREM H, LATTICE QUOTIENT OF PRISM(G) (proof by Fable, Independent Synthesis Review addendum A1; PI check; CLAIMED, both Claude family, cross-family review of step 4 requested). Statement: G 3-colourable, unpinned, H = Prism(G), r = rank L_G. Then L_H / M_H is canonically isomorphic to L_G / 3L_G, which is isomorphic to (Z/3)^r. This closes the open lower bound of 17911 (6c): [L_H : M_H] = 3^r exactly, not only 3^{rank_F3}. Proof outline (Fable): (1) Kempe swaps of H are global transpositions (17911 (6b)). So M_H = {sum delta_sigma n_sigma : delta_sigma in the augmentation ideal of Z[S3]}, and L_H / M_H = W / (W cap M_H), where W is the span of n_sigma - n_sigma0. (2) W is isomorphic to L_G via the injective linear gadget map x_sigma to n_sigma. (3) w in M_H iff there are a_sigma in Z[S3] with augmentation c_sigma and sum a_sigma n_sigma = 0. (4) Per vertex v put B_c = sum over sigma with sigma(v) = c of a_sigma, and M_c = m(B_c). Vanishing on the 7 gadget vertices and on R forces every M_c = (C_{v,c}/3) J, so 3 | C. (5) B_c = (C_c/3) E + t_c sgn. Read off at pi: C/3 + T for even pi and -T for odd pi, so C/3 is in L_G. The converse uses a_sigma = c'_sigma E. Hence W cap M_H corresponds to 3 L_G. PI check: step 4 is a finite local statement, the same for every v, and is decided by an exact rational kernel computation. Gadget table read off build_H, matching Fable's table up to row order: (012), (121), (202), (010), (122), (200), (011). The relation module has dimension 5 (2 from s_c with sum 0, 3 from sgn), and every M_c in it has equal columns (scratchpad/prism/thmH.py). Integrality of entries gives 3 | C_{v,c}. Steps 1, 2, 3 and 5 were checked by hand. Consistent with the exact index computations on 15 graphs (17911). Meaning: the Kempe lattice of Prism(G) carries no information beyond L_G mod 3. The prism readouts epsilon are injective on L_G/3L_G iff L_G is 3-saturated (prism graph: 7 of 8). No complexity content; no obligation closed.

structure.conclusion: (C1) Positive 1-in-3: S SAT iff the GF(3) solution set of {sum_{i in C} x_i = 1} contains a vector with <= 2 distinct values (j = all-ones is in the kernel; y - a j is Boolean). (C2) f_n = INCONS_n OR M_n with INCONS ideal of size N, so mSP_GF3(M_n) >= mSP_GF3(f_n) - N. (C3) Minimal GAP cores (Boolean-UNSAT, GF(3)-consistent, minimal) have GF(3)-independent rows, hence <= n-1 clauses, solution dimension n-|S|. Exact: n=6 900 cores (all size 5, 3 orbits), n=7 62,370 (8,190 size 5; 54,180 size 6). See theory/T44.

Generalization of the two-value criterion to positive 1-in-k over GF(p): (i) the all-ones vector j is in the kernel iff p | k (solutions form lines x + lambda j); (ii) a 0/1 vector with clause sums = 1 (mod p) has clause sums exactly 1 iff k <= p (sums lie in 0..k, next admissible value is 1+p). Hence 'S SAT iff Sol_p(S) contains a vector with <= 2 values' holds exactly for k = p: (3,3) and (5,5) yes; (4,2) no - GF(2) sees 'odd number true', not 'exactly one'; (3,2) no - j not in the kernel. GF(p)-blind MUS in the D-018 sense are defined only for k = p.

premises: One-way functions secure against non-uniform polynomial-size adversaries exist

structure.conclusion: W-D FIRST FAILING INFERENCE: (i) a polylogtime-uniform AC0 refuter has (log n)^{O(1)} alternating time per output bit, A has (log n)^{f(n)} state bits, f = omega(1): the refuter cannot simulate A, so it cannot search for a colliding pair. (ii) refuter outputs have circuit complexity <= c(log n)^c (CJSW Lemma 2.5): 2^{O((log n)^c log log n)} such prefixes versus 2^{(log n)^{f(n)}} states, so for f > c+1 counting forces NO collision among refuter-describable prefixes. Hence the uniform-collision obligation is exactly: no admissible A is injective on simple prefixes with (log n)^f-time updates - the update-cost (O*) obligation for DISJ (CJ4). Repair direction: non-injectivity from transition cost (route M update-map results S0036/S0037), not from counting.

statement: T54 sec.1-3 (theory/T54-graded-rees-deformation-boolean-ternary-2026-11-27.md). CLAIMED. R=F_p[t,X]/J, J=(x^2-tx) resp. (x^3-t^2x): graded, free over F_p[t], Rees algebra of the degree filtration, R/(t-1)=B, R/t=F_p[X]/(x^p) (KNOWN, standard). Lemma 1.2: g = f mod I => g^h = t^(deg g - deg fbar) fbar^h in R (Rees injectivity); I^h = J. Thm 2.2 (owner identity verified): z->ta is a well-defined algebra map since t^3(a^3-a)=0; sum_{a in F3^d} Q(X,ta,t) = (-t^2)^d [z^(2..2)]Q; C_Q homogeneous of degree D-2d, which is T52(b). Cor 2.3: the QE sum vanishes at t=0; C|_{t=0} = degree-e part of F, nonzero iff the T52 bound is tight. Prop 3.1: -[z^2] is a Frobenius form, det M(t)=1, perfect under every base change incl. t=0, Kronecker over tensors; t=1 counting pairing, t=0 socle pairing (known type: Euler/Tate trace). Evaluating it at t=1 is a counting (parity/Mod3) problem.
